feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Simultaneous return spillover networks and systemic risk among European banks
entry.summary: Contemporaneous Transmission Networks and Systemic Risk in European Banking arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper examines how contemporaneous equity-return transmission shapes systemic exposure among 51 listed European banks. Using a recursive non-Gaussian network model on volatility-standardized returns, the authors build two market-capitalization-weighted measures: the Systemic Impact Score, capturing a bank's influence on others, and the Systemic Vulnerability Score, capturing its exposure to shocks from elsewhere. The study also assesses the reproducibility of these roles and the limits of identification.

entry.title: Optimal quote placement for market makers under a state-dependent Hawkes order flow model
entry.summary: Optimal Order Placement under a State-Dependent Hawkes Process Limit Order Book model arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies how a market maker should place quotes when order flow follows a state-dependent Hawkes process. It links market-order counts to execution volumes through a block-based linear demand model and formulates a continuous-time, discrete-state dynamic program. Under a quadratic terminal inventory penalty, it derives inventory-dependent quotes and backward recursions for the value function coefficients. Numerical tests on LOBSTER data show higher aggregate terminal wealth than fixed-spread benchmarks at one and three ticks, but lower than the two-tick benchmark.

entry.title: Pricing Catastrophe Bonds in Incomplete Markets Using Riemannian Geometry and Financial Entropy
entry.summary: An Application of Geometric Riemannian Pricing Algorithm for Valuing Catastrophe Bonds in Incomplete Markets: Market-Consistent Financial Entropy and the Split of Frequency and Severity Risk Premia arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes a framework for pricing catastrophe bonds in incomplete markets by optimizing financial entropy with Riemannian geometry to select the pricing measure. It uses a compound Poisson and generalized Pareto loss model with Wang distortion and derives closed-form expressions for entropy and the Riemannian metric. Applied to a hypothetical earthquake bond calibrated to Golden State Re II (Series 2014-1) spreads, the study compares risk-neutral and physical trigger intensities and splits the risk premium between frequency and severity components.

entry.title: Deposits Should Not Reduce Returns: Supplier Income Monotonicity and Rate Curve Design in Pooled Lending
entry.summary: Depositing More Should Not Earn Less: Supplier Income Monotonicity and Rate Curve Design in Pooled Lending Markets arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies utilization-based interest rate models in which adding liquidity can lower a supplier's total interest income even as its balance rises. It gives the condition under which a supplier's income does not decrease with a marginal deposit and derives the resulting constraint on admissible rate curves. The authors also check how often the problematic case occurred on two public Drift markets.

entry.title: Simple, low-complexity ETF portfolios for private investors
entry.summary: Simple Portfolios that Deliver Consistent Decent Returns arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This empirical study tests portfolio construction methods for private investors using liquid US ETFs, with monthly trading costs and no short selling or leverage. The portfolios are built as convex optimization problems using interpretable inputs estimated from public data. The authors report that simple portfolios of as few as three ETFs deliver consistent returns and outperform a standard 60/40 allocation over the past two decades.

entry.title: Risk measures for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox-BESQ process
entry.summary: Risk measures for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox-BESQ process arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes an infinite-server queue model whose arrival intensity follows a Cox process driven by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Using the affine structure of the dynamics, it derives closed-form joint moment-generating functions for the arrival intensity, the number of customers, and the time integral of the customer count, extendable to two or more dates. These explicit functions are used to construct risk measures, such as joint moments conditional on a variable exceeding a threshold, computed via Fourier representations. Numerical experiments illustrate the practical implementation of the method.

entry.title: Event definition and branching ratio: Hawkes estimates of price-change clustering in consolidated quotes
entry.summary: Event definition and the branching ratio: Hawkes estimates of price-change clustering in the consolidated quote feed arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper fits Hawkes models to price changes in the consolidated US quote feed, where raw estimates show a sub-millisecond kernel and a near-critical branching ratio. The authors find that in large-tick stocks about half of NBBO changes are locked or depleted quotes resolved within a millisecond, which the model misreads as excitation. Defining events as a mid-price level persisting for one millisecond removes the sub-millisecond component.

entry.title: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge-Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment in Algorithmic Trading
entry.summary: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper proposes FinLLM-KG, a framework that combines causal large language models with a financial knowledge graph built from SEC 10-K filings. It supplies company-level context at inference time without updating model weights, either as a profile or as relevance-ranked factual triples. Sentiment scores are attributed to individual sentences and graph facts to make predictions more explainable. Simulations reportedly show consistent portfolio performance gains over a state-of-the-art baseline.

entry.title: Separating liquidity-driven from strategic loan defaults using deep learning
entry.summary: Disentangling Liquidity-Constrained from Strategic Default: A Deep Learning Approach arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper applies a deep neural network to a proprietary commercial mortgage panel from 1998 to 2021 to distinguish liquidity-constrained default from strategic default, two explanations for delinquency that are hard to tell apart with standard models. Among delinquent loans, property net operating income is found to matter more for default rates than loan-to-value. The estimated thresholds remain stable across the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 shock in 2020 and 2021.

entry.title: Modelling Regime Shifts in Electricity Intraday Markets with State-Dependent Hawkes Processes
entry.summary: Modelling Regime Shifts in Continuous Intraday Electricity Markets with State-dependent Hawkes Processes arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper proposes a multivariate state-dependent Hawkes process to model order flow across liquidity regimes in the continuous intraday electricity market. Market states are identified with a Liquidity Stress Index built from bid-ask spread, order book volume, and mid-price volatility. Calibrated on Dutch XBID hourly order data from EPEX SPOT for January-March 2024, the estimates show strongly self-exciting, near-critical order flow, with liquidity stress mainly strengthening same-side transaction self-excitation.

entry.title: FinAutoRubric: Expert-guided automatic rubric generation for evaluating financial research agents
entry.summary: FinAutoRubric: Expert-Guided Automatic Rubric Generation for Evaluating Financial Research Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents FinAutoRubric, a framework for evaluating finance research agents. Experts specify reusable evaluation guidance, and agents and code use it to generate, review, and validate query-specific rubrics, with reusable criteria stored in a Task Bank. On three expert-authored finance benchmarks, its rubrics match expert scoring about as closely as the strongest compared generator, agree with human grading, and were preferred by in-house analysts in blind review. The authors also release the 100-query FinAutoRubric Benchmark.

entry.title: LiveOption: Testing AI Agents on Structured Option Trading with Nonlinear Payoffs
entry.summary: LiveOption: Evaluating LLM Agents in Structured Option Trading with Nonlinear Payoffs arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper introduces LiveOption, a framework for evaluating large language model agents in option trading, a market more complex than simple stock trading. It provides a reproducible environment under realistic execution and capital constraints, covering portfolio overlays, earnings-event trading, and 0DTE intraday trading. The authors also propose a hierarchical metric suite assessing action validity, decision quality, risk, and outcomes. Experiments show current agents often fail to achieve competitive returns in most scenarios.

entry.title: RICE-Alpha: LLM Agent Stock Forecasting with Event Graphs and Reliability Correction
entry.summary: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents RICE-Alpha, a point-in-time stock-scoring framework that uses historical news events to forecast stock performance. It separates a multi-view base forecast from a reliability-calibrated residual correction based on how past events continued, using event graphs to preserve issuer-specific chronology. Tested on daily Nasdaq-100 and Hang Seng Index data from 2024 to 2026, it reportedly outperformed the evaluated LLM-based agents and momentum baselines. The authors conclude that historical event continuation adds information when it is temporally grounded, reliability-calibrated, and applied as a residual correction.

entry.title: Deep kernel hedging: a paper combining neural features with kernel methods for derivative hedging
entry.summary: Deep kernel hedging arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces a deep kernel hedging framework in which the hedging function lies in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose kernel is parameterized by a neural network embedding, and it handles path-dependent inputs via truncated time-augmented signature features. The authors derive a generalized representer theorem that reduces the empirical optimization to a finite-dimensional problem, and they use scalable random Fourier feature approximations with convergence guarantees. Experiments on synthetic and real data reportedly show competitive and robust hedging performance, especially in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: Applying Stated-Preference Economics to Evaluating Language Models
entry.summary: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper argues that the validity framework from stated-preference economics, covering content, construct, and criterion validity, reliability, incentive compatibility, and consequentiality, can evaluate language models when no correct answer exists. The authors test six models on a published water-quality stated-preference valuation survey (Vossler et al. 2023), using economic-theory predictions such as downward-sloping demand and willingness to pay responding to scope and income. Two older models fail the most basic test, while the two newest pass every scorable theoretical validity test but diverge on convergent validity. The authors stress that passing validity tests shows coherence, not correctness.

entry.title: Representation risk: pretrained image encoders can change predictive conclusions
entry.summary: Representation Risk in Pretrained Image Encoders arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper argues that the pretrained image encoder used to turn pictures into features is a source of model uncertainty, which the authors call representation risk. Ten frozen encoders were compared across tasks including house prices, racehorse performance, histology, chest radiographs, facial age, and rice disease, with the encoder chosen on locked validation data. The results show no single encoder is best everywhere, and the authors recommend benchmarking candidates, selecting on validation data, and reporting paired and split-level uncertainty. The workflow is implemented in the LOOKAGAIN-ML software package. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes representation risk, showing that ten frozen image encoders across six applications yield large validation-selected test gaps, e.g., house-price R² rising from 0.396 to 0.629.

entry.title: A spread-gated Hawkes model of best bid and ask dynamics, applied to limit order sizing
entry.summary: A Spread-Gated Hawkes-Flocking Model for Best Bid and Ask Dynamics, with an Application to Limit Order Placement arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper models the joint dynamics of the best bid and ask prices with a spread-gated Hawkes-flocking process that distinguishes four types of best-quote movements and includes a spread-dependent cross-side excitation term. The authors prove non-explosion on finite horizons, provide an O(N) recursive likelihood, and validate maximum likelihood estimation by simulation. On intraday data for INTC and MSFT, removing the cross-side term is rejected and the full model fits substantially better by AIC and BIC. As an application, they derive a closed-form optimal size for a single-period limit order placed at the best or second-best quote.

entry.title: When Hedging Changes the Payoff: Option Replication Under Price Impact and Trading Costs
entry.summary: When Hedging Changes the Payoff: Option Replication with Price Impact and Execution Costs arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies how hedging a derivative by trading the underlying asset can change the payoff it was meant to replicate, once trading causes price impact and execution costs. In a binomial model replication is characterized by a fixed-point equation, and in continuous time a nonlinear pricing PDE is derived. For monotone convex Lipschitz payoffs such as calls and puts, exact replication is established under midpoint execution costs, and numerical experiments illustrate the effects.

entry.title: Comparing two ways to split tail risk among components
entry.summary: A tale of two allocations: Risk capital contributions versus risk contributions in the tail arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper compares two proportional measures of how much each risk component contributes to aggregate tail risk: the share of tail risk capital allocated under Conditional Tail Expectation (CTE), and the expected realized risk share under Geometric Tail Expectation (GTE). It establishes when the two allocations agree, how they are ordered when they differ, and how they separate asymptotically in the extreme tail. The difference is shown to be a normalized tail covariance.</summary>

entry.title: Testing whether a Pepsi–Coca-Cola pairs trade still works after its original fit period.
entry.summary: From Cointegration to Out-of-Sample Failure: A Pairs-Trading Case Study on PEP-KO arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper tests whether a pairs trading strategy between PepsiCo and The Coca-Cola Company, based on cointegration, is statistically robust and economically exploitable. The authors estimate the spread's mean-reversion parameters over 2013–2018, fix them, and optimise a threshold trading strategy in-sample over 2018–2023. The strategy is assessed with transaction-cost and parameter sensitivity tests, walk-forward validation, and adjusted and deflated Sharpe ratios, then evaluated out-of-sample from 2023 onward. The results show that weakening mean-reversion in the spread undermines the strategy's out-of-sample effectiveness.

entry.title: Optimal Liquidation Near Support and Resistance under Multi-Skew Brownian Motion
entry.summary: Optimal Liquidation with Support and Resistance Levels under Multi-Skew Brownian Motion arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper solves a perpetual liquidation problem for a geometric multi-skew Brownian motion with local-time pushes at a support level and a resistance level, a technical-analysis-style model that depends only on price. A closed-form criterion yields three geometries: the continuation band lies below resistance, straddles it, or has its upper edge at resistance. Selling into resistance emerges as a conclusion rather than an assumption. Support parameters are identified exactly from exercise behaviour, while resistance strength is identifiable only within an interval with a closed-form endpoint.

entry.title: Oracle-parametrized AMMs: pricing rules that use external price feeds
entry.summary: Oracle-Parametrized Constant Function Market Makers: From Price Feeds to Pricing Rules arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper introduces oracle-parametrized automated market makers (OP-AMMs), whose quoted prices depend on both pool reserves and an external oracle price, suited to settings like tokenized securities where price discovery happens off-chain. Under a strict oracle-contraction condition, the authors show the quoted price lies between the oracle price and an implicit autarkic price set by the reserves, and derive a loss-versus-rebalancing decomposition. The analysis extends to stale and discrete-update oracles and sandwich attacks, and a backtest on one-second SPY NBBO data illustrates the trade-offs.

entry.title: CZAR Loss: A Loss Function Designed for Financial Log-Return Prediction
entry.summary: Introducing the CZAR Loss: A Tailored Objective Function for Financial Log-Return Predictions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper argues that standard symmetric regression losses, such as mean squared and mean absolute error, are poorly aligned with financial return prediction, since they make a constant zero forecast nearly optimal and penalize models with weak directional skill. It introduces the CZAR (Composite Zero-Agnostic Return) loss, a piecewise quadratic function that is convex in the prediction and has closed-form gradient and Hessian for use in gradient-boosted libraries. In idealized tests and a LightGBM experiment on intraday BTC log-returns, the authors report reduced zero-returns bias and better directional accuracy on large-magnitude returns.

entry.title: RADAR: Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion for Portfolio Optimization with Stochastic Discount Factors
entry.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Modeling for Stochastic Discount Factor Portfolios arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies portfolio optimization within the stochastic discount factor framework by learning market state representations that capture underlying financial risk structures. The authors propose RADAR, which retrieves similar historical market regimes to build context-dependent noise distributions and applies conditional diffusion to denoise multimodal inputs. The authors report state-of-the-art results on key risk-adjusted metrics and economically meaningful signals for asset returns and correlations.

entry.title: From Word Counts to Context: Topic Models for Asset Pricing
entry.summary: From Word Counts to Context: Topic Models for Asset Pricing arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper compares a sentence transformer with k-means clustering against Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for generating topics from 394,661 news articles used in a financial portfolio construction pipeline. Topic coherence is measured by NPMI and financial performance by the Sharpe ratio. The sentence transformer approach shows higher observed scores on both measures, though the authors note the tests do not establish outperformance. They suggest stricter tests using only information available at each date, and broader datasets, are needed.

entry.title: Controlling Option Greeks: Portfolios with Built-in Hedging Bias
entry.summary: Taming the Greeks: Option Portfolios with Inductive Biases arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents an end-to-end deep learning framework for systematic options trading that embeds hedging behavior by explicitly controlling portfolio-level risk exposures. It adds a differentiable risk-sensitivity penalty to the training objective to keep portfolios neutral on selected risk dimensions, trained on historical data. Tests on Nasdaq 100 equity options report that a well-calibrated penalty improves out-of-sample risk-adjusted performance and reduces realized directional exposure compared with an unregularized baseline.

entry.title: EverMine: Studying Self-Evolving Research Skills in Long-Term Alpha Discovery
entry.summary: EverMine: Dissecting the Self-Evolution of Research Capabilities in Long-Horizon Alpha Research arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper introduces EverMine, a framework for testing whether self-evolving agents keep improving their accumulated research skills during long-horizon alpha factor discovery. It splits the research state into history, the current factor portfolio, and reusable capabilities, and compares runs with fixed or evolving capabilities under matched resource limits. Across 18 long trajectories and 48 continuation branches, capability evolution showed no consistent gain, while tuning existing factor structures still helped. The authors also find that a candidate's value depends on the evolving portfolio and the order in which candidates are submitted.

entry.title: How much screening can offset slower quote updates for liquidity providers
entry.summary: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 The paper studies the spread a liquidity provider needs to break even when counterparties can exploit stale quotes, comparing faster repricing with screening of informed flow on one scale. Empirically, across four USDC-WETH pools benchmarked against Binance ETH-USDT, one-second price innovations are sharply non-Gaussian, with 73% of seconds showing no price change. Moving from twelve-second to one-second cadence sheds 84.5% of the expected shock, so a twelve-second maker must screen at least that share of informed flow to match. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a break-even condition placing repricing speed and informed-flow screening on one scale; on four USDC-WETH pools, 73% of one-second shocks are zero and a 12-second maker must screen a

entry.title: Efficient frontier computed with a standard LASSO solver
entry.summary: The Efficient Frontier from a LASSO Solver arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This note numerically checks Schmelzer and Hastie's result that Markowitz's Critical Line Algorithm and the LASSO path trace the same curve, using scikit-learn's lars_path with no portfolio software. It tests long-short portfolios under a leverage cap, fixed leverage with varying risk appetite, and the classical long-only fully invested frontier, and reports agreement with independent quadratic-programming solvers. The script, checks, Fama-French returns and an R cross-check are published so the results can be reproduced.

entry.title: Non-perturbative option pricing for rough volatility using quantum-field-theory effective action
entry.summary: Dyson-Schwinger Effective-Action Methods for Rough Volatility: A Correlation-Response Architecture for Calibration, Exotics and Risk arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper proposes a non-perturbative framework for stochastic-volatility option pricing based on the two-particle-irreducible effective action and Dyson-Schwinger gap equations. It approximates the joint law of state variables with a self-consistent Gaussian and handles both Markovian and rough (Volterra) models, including nonzero correlation. Reported benchmarks show close agreement with Monte Carlo references and comparisons against Hagan's expansion and rough SABR.

entry.title: Buying at support: optimal entry under multi-skew Brownian price motion
entry.summary: Buying at Support: The Entry Problem under Multi-Skew Brownian Motion arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 The paper studies when to buy a share that will later be sold optimally, when the price follows a geometric multi-skew Brownian motion whose skew levels represent support and resistance. The buying reward is the exit premium from a companion liquidation problem. The entry problem reduces to a finite one, and with one support and one resistance, the optimal rule is to buy exactly at the support, with an explicit value.

entry.title: Robust enhanced index tracking portfolio selection under uncertain return distributions
entry.summary: Robust enhanced index tracking portfolio selection under distributional uncertainty arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies building portfolios that aim to beat a benchmark index when the true joint distribution of asset and index losses is unknown. The authors propose robust models, guided by Pareto-optimality, that minimize a convex combination of worst-case mean loss and downside risk under a worst-case mean return constraint. Empirical tests on real market data report better out-of-sample cumulative wealth and Sharpe, Sortino, and Omega ratios than the tracked index, an equal-weighted portfolio, and other robust models.

entry.title: Cities of Signals: Compression and Novelty Geometry Explained
entry.summary: Cities of Signals: Compression, Separation, and the Geometry of Novelty arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper treats each daily cross-sectional forecast as a point on a sphere and defines its "city" as the direction of its time-averaged vector, a compressed summary of signal history. It proves probability bounds on when the angle between two cities conservatively estimates the angle between their histories. The authors test these results on positive-IC signal pairs from AlphaNova's May 2026 competition, finding agreement that is mostly positive but not fully explained by the uniform null model.

entry.title: Optimal design of catastrophe bonds and their use for climate change risk
entry.summary: Optimal Catastrophe Bond Design and its Applications to Climate Change Risk arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper treats the payout function of catastrophe bonds as a decision variable and studies their optimal design from the sponsor's perspective. It shows that a piecewise linear indemnity function is optimal under expected-disutility and spectral-risk-measure frameworks, reducing the design problem to a one-dimensional choice of attachment point. Calibrated with U.S. severe storm loss data, the optimal designs are reported to achieve substantial risk reductions across most risk criteria.

entry.title: Stochastic Knothe-Rosenblatt: fast calibration of stochastic local volatility models
entry.summary: Stochastic Knothe-Rosenblatt: Light-speed Calibration of Stochastic Local Volatility Models arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper notes that European option smiles pin down an asset's risk-neutral marginal distributions but not how they are linked across maturities. It proposes a modular calibration overlay for existing stochastic and path-dependent volatility models, building a martingale that exactly matches all prescribed marginals while staying as close as possible to the reference dynamics in an adapted Knothe-Rosenblatt sense. The authors cover numerical implementation, convergence to the SLV model, benchmarks on Heston and Bergomi dynamics, and a multi-asset extension.

entry.title: Axient: A canonical protocol graph for leveraged event markets with single-authority state and recoverable execution
entry.summary: Axient: Canonical Protocol-Graph Composition for Leveraged Event Markets: Single State Authority, Atomic Composition, Durable Sagas, and Exactly-Once Recovery arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper addresses leveraged event-market protocols, where individually correct contracts may still lack a single authoritative financial execution path. It proposes a canonical protocol graph in which each financial domain has one storage authority and composition components coordinate transitions. The authors formally prove properties such as atomic closure, loss conservation and priority, and exactly-once recovery, and evaluate the implementation through twelve Financial Interaction Assertions and a reproducible evidence chain.

entry.title: Social welfare and price discovery in double auction markets explained
entry.summary: Social welfare and price discovery in double auction markets arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 Double auctions are known from lab experiments to drive prices toward competitive equilibrium, but no theory explained this. The paper studies dynamic double auctions in a pure exchange economy where agents bid indifference prices implied by their holdings and preferences. It shows that Walras equilibria coincide with the fixed points of the double auction, and that repeated auctions produce bounded sequences of allocations and prices whose cluster points are Walras equilibria with transfers.

entry.title: Shared Models, Selective Trading, and Order Flow: A study of whether diverse language models still differ in the orders they submit when news framing changes in synthetic markets.
entry.summary: Shared Models, Selective Trading, and Order Flow arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper uses synthetic markets with a fixed mix of three language-model families to examine how news presentation affects the orders they submit. It reports that Qwen's share of submitted orders shifted by 48 percentage points in a financing event with little change in net order counts, and Mistral's share shifted by 40 points in a workforce-reduction event where net counts reversed sign. An analytical decomposition shows selection can improve or worsen price accuracy even when aggregate demand sensitivity is unchanged.

entry.title: Spouse-Protected Tontines: A Retirement Pool That Keeps Paying the Surviving Spouse
entry.summary: Spouse-Protected Tontines: Household Decumulation via Neural-Network Optimization arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper proposes a tontine design in which the first death in a household does not transfer money to the pool; instead, the account continues to pay the surviving spouse. The authors set up a multidimensional withdrawal and rebalancing problem that trades off expected real payments against the CVaR of terminal shortfalls, solved with a neural-network policy parameterization. Numerical experiments calibrated to Australia show the spouse-only phase is a first-order, persistent household event, and that book-level diversification removes most of the excess upper-tail cost of spouse continuation.

entry.title: Multi-period bond portfolio optimization with transaction costs via a Markov Decision Process
entry.summary: Multiperiod bond portfolio optimization with transaction costs using a Markov Decision process arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper addresses how bank treasury portfolios should allocate across bonds of different maturities under interest-rate risk, noting that static allocations can suffer large losses when rates rise. It proposes a simulation-based multi-period framework that models yield curves with a Dynamic Nelson-Siegel parameterization and vector autoregressive factor dynamics, approximated by a discrete-state Markov chain. Within a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process with proportional rebalancing costs, the investor maximizes expected terminal wealth, with the optimal policy found by backward induction. The authors also quantify the error from truncating the transition kernel, finding that mean terminal wealth is barely affected while drawdown and tail statistics are substantially distorted.

entry.title: AlphaPADI: Automatically discovering stock prediction formulas by generating formula pools with diffusion
entry.summary: AlphaPADI: Formulaic Alpha Discovery via Pool-Aware Hierarchical Discrete Diffusion arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies formulaic alpha discovery, which seeks symbolic formulas that predict cross-sectional stock returns. The authors propose AlphaPADI, a framework with grammar-constrained buffer initialization, pool-aware hierarchical discrete diffusion, and reward-guided pool refinement that considers both predictive performance and diversity among formulas. According to the paper, experiments on Chinese and U.S. stock markets show AlphaPADI outperforms the evaluated baselines in predictive and portfolio performance.

entry.title: Comparing learned and hand-crafted monotone temporal risk aggregation under equal admissibility
entry.summary: Measuring Learned Monotone Temporal Aggregation at Matched Admissibility arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 The paper studies risk scores that must be monotone non-decreasing in every exposure input, a constraint drawn from financial regulation. The authors build a recurrent network whose state uses classical risk statistics, keeping it monotone, and compare it with hand-crafted aggregates under the same constraint. They find that learned and engineered aggregation are substitutes within the separable family, but the learned approach fails on consecutivity, time localization, and the exposure floor. Each incumbent approach has advantages on different axes, and none dominates on all three.

entry.title: Stock-JEPA: Learning Equity Market Representations by Revising a Financial Prior
entry.summary: STOCK-JEPA: Prior-Anchored Latent Revision Representation Learning in Equity Markets arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper proposes Stock-JEPA, a framework for learning representations from low signal-to-noise equity market data. It anchors a latent space to fixed statistics from a simple financial model describing multi-horizon returns and risk, then learns a context-based predictor of the revision needed to reach future representations. The authors report that it outperforms 13 baselines on China and U.S. equity universes across five evaluation metrics.

entry.title: FactorBench: A Portfolio-Aware Benchmark for Automated Factor Mining
entry.summary: FactorBench: A Portfolio-Aware Benchmark for Automated Factor Mining arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper introduces FactorBench, a benchmark that compares about 5,000 factors produced by nine automated mining methods across five equity markets. It evaluates factor validity, temporal generalization, predictiveness beyond risk and style exposures, pool distinctness including similarity to Alpha101, and the quality of composite signals and after-cost portfolio performance. The authors find that no single mining paradigm consistently outperforms the others.

entry.title: Explaining Neural Calibration of Volatility Models Using Shapley Values
entry.summary: Shapley-based Structural Analysis of Neural Calibration for Stochastic Volatility Models arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper uses two complementary Shapley-based explainable AI methods, SHAP and νSHAP, to analyze neural network calibration of the Heston and rough Heston stochastic volatility models. It compares several architectures and finds that short maturities and smile wings dominate parameter inference, with a stable attribution pattern across architectures. The authors show that νSHAP explanations can guide a large reduction in input dimensionality for the rough Heston model while keeping calibration accuracy comparable to using the full implied volatility surface.

entry.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Splitting Trade Mix from Event Picking
entry.summary: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper argues that financial LLM agents are often judged by return differences against a baseline, which cannot tell event-selection skill apart from passive market exposure. The authors propose an audit that keeps each type of action change at its observed count and randomly reassigns them across eligible events, using the average payoff as a composition benchmark. Applied to 723 earnings events at 44 U.S. consumer-facing firms, the agent's gross value of +15.2 bps per event splits into a +25.8 composition benchmark and a -10.6 selection value, showing no detectable outperformance over matched random assignment.

entry.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in a Solved Broker-Trader Game
entry.summary: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper places a proximal policy optimisation (PPO) agent in an analytically solved continuous-time broker-trader game, where it chooses the broker's trading speed. With stochastic uninformed order flow, the tested PPO networks remain inaccurate, and their critics do not reliably rank nearby actions. Under partial information, a causal certainty-equivalent controller based on observable history stays closer to the reference than PPO. Freezing the analytical policy and training PPO to adjust it after a cost change closes 2.22% of the gap to the changed-cost reference.

entry.title: FinNextAssist: A Deep Research Assistant for Professional Finance
entry.summary: FinNextAssist: Towards Professional Financial Deep Research Assistant arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents FinNextAssist, an end-to-end deep research framework for professional financial analysis. It splits the research process into four stages: task planning, evidence compilation, reasoning, and report assembly, and adds two lightweight sub-agents, TabAgent for cross-market financial table understanding and HeteroAgent for interpreting heterogeneous financial data across modalities. The authors report experiments on three benchmarks showing it outperforms strong proprietary and open-source deep research agents, with ablations confirming each component's contribution.

entry.title: MintEval: Do LLMs Build the Trading Strategy Requested? A Behaviour-Matching Benchmark for Language-to-Strategy Code
entry.summary: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper introduces MintEval, a benchmark that checks whether code generated by large language models from plain-language trading descriptions behaves like the strategy requested. Generated and reference programs are run bar by bar on identical market data and frictions, and compared by their trading actions rather than code similarity or profit. The results show that even a frontier model silently fails on a substantial share of tasks, and that an existing LLM judge accepts all of these failures. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes MintEval, a bar-by-bar behavioural-equivalence benchmark for LLM-generated trading strategy code; the authors report 79.2% of correctly read implementations diverge on over 10% of active bars

entry.title: Event History Over Scale: Compact Transformers for Low-Latency Order Book Forecasting
entry.summary: Event History Over Scale: Compact Transformers for Low-Latency Limit Order Book Forecasting arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper introduces MBOFormer, a 7,203-parameter causal transformer, and MBOFusion, a 14,371-parameter extension with a slow temporal-context branch, for short-horizon price-trend prediction from limit order books. Both models use market-by-order (level-3) histories of order submissions, cancellations, and executions, and are compared with level-2 snapshot-based baselines. The authors report the highest mean macro-F1 in eleven of twelve settings across three markets and four horizons, with sub-millisecond median inference and state dictionaries under 70 kB.

entry.title: Multi-agent AI as a nested principal-agent problem in private wealth management across Switzerland, Germany and Austria
entry.summary: Multi-Agent AI as a Nested Principal-Agent Problem in Private Wealth Management: Mandate Representation and Evidence Control in Switzerland, Germany and Austria arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper proposes a model-independent framework that combines nested principal-agent delegation, in which a manager hands work to AI acting for the client, with constrained joint maximisation of client and manager outcomes. Legal duties, mandate requirements and evidence sufficiency determine admissibility, with Switzerland, Germany and Austria as the legal context. Simulations using constructed mandates and public-market data show how weights and omitted terms can change selected services. These are illustrative examples, and professional and field studies are needed to assess oversight and client outcomes.

entry.title: Axient: A Manifest-Bound Evidence Framework for On-Chain Financial Protocols
entry.summary: Axient: Manifest-Bound Evidence for On-Chain Financial Protocols: Seven-Layer Derivation, Correlation, Tamper Rejection, and Reproducible Claim Promotion arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents an evidence architecture for hybrid on-chain financial protocols, in which a sealed execution manifest binds system identities, roles, schemas and release identity. Seven evidence layers are linked by a common correlation identity and must satisfy a conjunctive rule before a claim is promoted. The authors formalize the evidence graph, prove that copied hashes cannot establish independent derivation, and report a registered local case study showing a reviewable chain from financial assertions to a replay-bound package.

entry.title: Same Ranking, Different Scale: Checking LLM Judges for Job-Related AI Measurement
entry.summary: Right Order, Wrong Scale: Auditing LLM Judges for Occupational AI Measurement arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper introduces O*NET-BENCH, an audit suite built from an existing survey of 45,796 worker ratings, to test 33 LLM judge configurations on whether AI responses meet workplace requirements. Many judges agree with human raters on response rankings, yet their estimated acceptance rates range from 3.0% to 97.9%, compared with 61.1% for occupation-matched workers. The authors conclude that ranking agreement alone is insufficient for occupational measurement and that judges should be validated against the acceptance rates and aggregates they will be used to estimate.

entry.title: Expected Utility Regret Rule: Minimax and Bayes-Optimal Portfolio Selection
entry.summary: Expected Utility Regret Rule: Minimax and Bayes Optimal Portfolio Choice arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies portfolio choice, aiming to recommend portfolios that maximize an investor's expected utility of wealth. It proposes the Expected Utility Regret (EUR) rule, which jointly selects a portfolio class and estimates its weights. In a regular parametric return model, a single EUR rule attains both minimax and Bayes lower bounds without using the prior distribution. Mean-variance and risk-parity portfolios are shown to be special cases of this framework. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an EUR rule that, without a prior, reportedly attains both minimax and Bayes regret lower bounds including leading constants, recovering mean-variance and risk-parity portfolios as

entry.title: Verifying Agent Claims by Evidence, Not Aggregate Scores
entry.summary: Verify Claims, Not Scores: Evidence-Based Verification of Modular Agents arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper proposes a claim-specific verification audit for modular agents that plan, act, check and refine, scoring the evidence behind each conclusion rather than an overall task score. Each conclusion receives one of four verdicts (supported, unsupported, unresolved, or not evaluated) along with its supporting evidence and scope. The authors apply oracle policies and component replacement to a constrained portfolio-allocation agent in a synthetic market with hidden regimes. The main contribution is the protocol itself, and the empirical findings apply only to the agent and environment studied.

entry.title: PPO-HRAP: A Risk-Controlled Trading Policy Blending PPO with Regime-Aware Exposure
entry.summary: PPO-HRAP: Proximal Policy Optimization with a Hybrid Regime-Aware Policy for Risk-Controlled Trading arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper proposes PPO-HRAP, a reinforcement learning trading method that combines Proximal Policy Optimization with an interpretable, volatility-aware regime prior. Its reward blends portfolio log return, a VIX-conditioned drawdown penalty, target-exposure deviation, and turnover cost. On a held-out 2020-2022 SPY test window, it reports 27.62% total return and reduces maximum drawdown from 34.10% (Buy and Hold) to 18.47%. The authors note high turnover remains, and cross-asset results on QQQ and DIA are single-run only.

entry.title: Pricing American options under stochastic local volatility and stochastic correlation using RBSDEs
entry.summary: On the Pricing of American Options under Stochastic Local Volatility and Stochastic Correlation via the RBSDE Framework arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies American option pricing in stochastic local volatility (SLV) models extended with stochastic correlation driven by an additional stochastic process. The authors derive the corresponding reflected forward-backward stochastic differential equations (RBSDEs) and solve them with data-driven numerical methods for pricing and hedging. They also provide a convergence analysis of the method and numerical experiments assessing the extended models and the accuracy and efficiency of the approach.

entry.title: Beyond Supra-Competitive Outcomes: Collusive Behaviour in Deep RL Trading Games
entry.summary: Beyond Supra-Competitive Outcomes: Collusive Behaviour in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Execution Games arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies a two-player, finite-horizon liquidation game in which independent reinforcement learning agents reach costs below the Nash benchmark. The authors identify a learned punishment mechanism: when one agent deviates, the other accelerates liquidation, costing the deviator more than it gains while leaving the punisher's average payoff largely unchanged. Two formal checks show the punishment outweighs the deviation gain and that the change in trading explains the loss, supporting a collusive interpretation.

entry.title: QuantCode Model: Language Models for Executable Trading Code
entry.summary: QuantCode Model: Specializing Language Models for Executable Algorithmic Trading Code arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how to adapt large language models to turn natural-language trading strategy descriptions into executable Backtrader code. The authors compare continued pretraining on trading-framework code with supervised fine-tuning on agent-validated request-to-code pairs, evaluated on the 400-task QuantCode-Bench. Supervised fine-tuning gave the larger gain, raising Judge Pass for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B to 58.2%. The authors also report that domain specialization can degrade structured tool-calling ability, which targeted recovery training partly restores.|

entry.title: Rank Collapse of the Predictor Jacobian in Decision-Focused Learning
entry.summary: Jacobian Rank Collapse in Decision-Focused Learning arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how a rank restriction in the predictor Jacobian limits the parameter-update directions available in decision-focused learning (DFL). Rank-one Jacobians make per-example gradients nearly collinear, and the authors show that such local statements do not imply common minimizers or collinear batch updates. In experiments, DFL gains over MSE stayed below 1.8% in 38 equity configurations, while full-capacity SPO+ reduced regret in shortest-path and knapsack tasks, with only the knapsack result surviving multiple-comparison correction.

entry.title: Say, Echo, Do: Strategic Narratives and Revealed Positioning in Financial Markets
entry.summary: Say, Echo, Do: Strategic Narratives and Revealed Positioning in Financial Markets arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how institutional statements (Say), media repetition (Echo), and actual trading positions (Do) relate in financial markets, asking when text signals should be followed or faded. A linear-quadratic model identifies when an informed institution talks an asset down while buying it. The authors propose methods to detect echo articles, learn return-aligned embeddings, and measure who moved first. In simulated markets with known ground truth, echo sentiment predicted returns with a significantly negative sign in all 29 markets.

entry.title: A Generalized Langevin Model of Latent Liquidity and Concave Price Impact
entry.summary: A Generalized Langevin Model of Latent Liquidity and Concave Price Impact arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper models market impact as the response to submitted order flow net of counterflow from latent traders, who become active when price moves exceed their individual thresholds. Order flow depletes this latent pool, whose recovery follows a generalized Langevin equation with memory over several time scales. For an undepleted pool, the model yields an intermediate square-root regime between linear small- and large-order limits without assuming a square-root law directly. Numerical experiments show that depletion narrows this regime, and calibration to market data is deferred to a companion paper.

entry.title: Information Games: How Rivalry Reshapes Firm Positioning in Language-Model Space
entry.summary: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper introduces ESCAPE, a rational-share game in which firms with different capability costs position themselves in a language-model representation space, and proves a unique equilibrium. It derives an exact reallocation formula separating opportunity effects from crowding effects, showing that competition need not push firms apart. Rivalry mainly changes how differently firms respond to the same opportunity shift. Corporate news data show that peer structure is persistent but changes over time.

entry.title: From Intraday Orderbook to Imbalance Price: How Cross-Market Trading Shapes Balancing Prices
entry.summary: From Intraday Orderbook to Imbalance Price: Understanding Cross-Market Interaction arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 As variable renewables make power scheduling more uncertain, this paper uses probabilistic modeling to study how intraday orderbook information reflects later imbalance price formation in Germany and Austria. It compares orderbook representations such as VWAP and last mid price, including neighboring products and products from the neighboring country. The authors find VWAP with neighboring products performs best in both countries, while adding fundamental features reduces test loss in Germany but increases it in Austria.

entry.title: Det-MASO: Diversity-Regularized Multi-Agent Sequential Optimization for Factor Generation
entry.summary: Det-MASO: Diversity-Regularized Multi-Agent Sequential Optimization for Factor Generation arXiv · Oct 26, 2026 This paper proposes Det-MASO, a framework for generating alpha factors in quantitative investing. It adds a differentiable log-determinant penalty on the inter-agent correlation matrix to the joint objective, discouraging agents from producing similar outputs while keeping computational cost linear in the number of assets. The authors report that the method outperforms baselines and improves the Sharpe ratio by 0.33.

entry.title: Do round-number prices act as barriers? Order book study of liquidity and price departures
entry.summary: Do Round Numbers Hold Prices? Occupation Densities and Depth-Conditioned Hazards in the Limit Order Book arXiv · Oct 26, 2026 Prices often cluster at round numbers, which is sometimes read as evidence those levels act as barriers. This paper uses limit order book data and a tick-grid framework to separate barrier effects from a mechanical explanation, where deeper resting liquidity makes prices slower to leave. Analyzing five Nasdaq stocks throughout 2025, it finds round levels attract more liquidity but do not show longer depth-adjusted durations. Intel and SoFi show directional effects, with departures biased away from round levels.

entry.title: Finite bid-ask spread from replenishment placed away from the quote
entry.summary: A Finite Bid--Ask Spread from Replenishment Displaced from the Quote arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper gives an analytic account of a finite bid-ask spread in a two-field reaction-diffusion order book model that tracks bid and ask densities over operational time. A market-making source withholds order placement over a finite interval around the reaction boundary, representing replenishment displaced from the quote. Under a quasistationary, weak-overlap approximation, the quoted spread is the sub-threshold core of the placement-free interval. Market orders remove density at the quote, while replenishment arrives outside it and must diffuse back, producing a delayed and attenuated quote-level response.

entry.title: A functional representation of credit behavior for default probability modeling
entry.summary: A Functional Representation of Credit Behavior for Probability of Default Modeling arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper proposes a framework that models probability of default using functional data analysis, representing credit variables as continuous functions. It shows that commonly used variables such as available funds, utilization rate, and overdraft can be derived from three time-observed quantities: account type, account balance, and credit limit. A relative time framework aligns recurring banking-day cycles across borrowers, and the approach is evaluated with functional logistic regression. The model reportedly matches XGBoost's predictive performance while outperforming standard logistic regression and retaining the interpretability of linear models.

entry.title: Ex ante and scenario-conditional value of information in dynamic portfolio choice
entry.summary: Ex Ante and Scenario-Conditional Value of Information in Dynamic Portfolio Choice arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies portfolio decisions under uncertainty about expected returns, where investors update beliefs as new information arrives. It introduces scenario-conditional expected utility and value of information, comparing a fixed-belief investor, a price observer, and an attentive investor with limited attention capacity in a finite-horizon Gaussian model. Ex ante, learning and attention are valuable, but scenario-conditionally learning brings both a correction benefit and a fluctuation cost, so the ranking can reverse.

entry.title: Tail instability and scale control in neural network models that generate Treasury yield scenarios
entry.summary: Tail Instability and Scale Control in Conditional Normalizing Flows for Treasury Yield-Curve Scenarios arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper compares two conditional normalizing flow models that generate scenarios for daily changes in eleven Treasury yield maturities. On a new 60-date window, the original model produced extreme samples with an absolute standardized coordinate of 34.3 million, while a stabilized Gaussian-base version reached 14.72. The authors find that numerical stability did not translate into better prediction, as historical simulation scored better on distributional measures and coverage on the new window.

entry.title: Diffusive Market Impact: A Consistent Microfoundation
entry.summary: Diffusive Market Impact: A Consistent Microfoundation arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper provides a microfoundation for diffusive market impact, which explains the square-root law of market impact and its shift to a linear regime at low trading rates. In a model with one trader and many arbitrageurs who progressively eliminate predictable returns, impact returns become white. The authors also discuss the economic meaning of the impact phase and find that under a biexponential trade flow, impact decline falls within a 50%–60% band.

entry.title: Realized Tail-Risk Expectile Models for Stable, Accurate VaR and ES Forecasts
entry.summary: Realized Tail-Risk Conditional Autoregressive Expectile Models: Accurate and Stable Forecasting Performance arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper proposes a realized tail-risk conditional autoregressive expectile (RTCARE) model for jointly forecasting value-at-risk (VaR) and expected shortfall (ES). It adds realized tail measures, such as realized quantile and realized ES built from intraday high-frequency returns, to the dynamics and measurement equations of the conditional expectile. Parameters are estimated by Markov chain Monte Carlo, and forecasts are assessed in numerical examples and an empirical study using U.S. stock returns. The RTCARE models perform competitively and often better than existing alternatives across the tail levels considered, with stable results across Monte Carlo replications and rolling forecast evaluations.

entry.title: Adding transaction-text behavioural features to credit risk scorecards
entry.summary: Enhancing credit risk scorecards with transactional-based behavioural features arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper examines whether payment narratives in transaction data can serve as an alternative source for credit risk modelling. Using natural language processing and regular expressions, the authors convert unstructured transaction descriptions into interpretable spending categories with a newly developed classification algorithm. Adding these features to a scorecard significantly increased its Gini coefficient compared with a scorecard without them.

entry.title: Entropy-regularized dynamic portfolio selection under no-shorting constraints
entry.summary: Entropy Regularization under No-Shorting: Structure Preservation and Convexity in Dynamic Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper studies entropy regularization for discrete-time dynamic mean-variance portfolio selection with no-shorting constraints. It introduces a state-dependent temperature matched to the problem's homogeneity, which preserves the piecewise-quadratic value function and finite-dimensional Bellman recursion. The authors prove that a sufficiently small common temperature keeps the Bellman structure and convexity over the whole finite horizon, and the original solution is recovered as the temperature vanishes.

entry.title: Using a supervised neural network to initialize reinforcement learning for timing exits from SPX short-straddle options
entry.summary: MLP-Initialized Reinforcement Learning for Exit Timing in SPX Short-Straddle Portfolios arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper studies when to exit SPX short-straddle option portfolios using two stages. A multilayer perceptron is first trained on ex-post optimal hold or exit labels from historical data, then used to initialize reinforcement-learning actors fine-tuned with a risk-aware trading reward. Out-of-sample tests over 2024 to 2026 show the supervised MLP substantially outperforms passive holding and fixed-time or profit-and-loss exit rules.

entry.title: FLEX Options and Market Outcomes: How Customized Exchange-Traded Options Affect Regular Options and Stocks
entry.summary: FOMO: FLEX Options and Market Outcomes arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper examines whether activity in FLEX options, exchange-cleared contracts with customizable strikes, expirations, exercise styles and settlement terms, leaves measurable effects on regular listed options and underlying equities. Using data from March 2025 to March 2026 covering 41 underlyings and 53 event dates, the authors find a significant post-event rise in listed-option open interest and show FLEX activity concentrates in high implied-volatility environments. They conclude FLEX activity mainly serves as an observable marker of institutional volatility demand and open-interest positioning rather than a predictor of stock returns.

entry.title: Funding Debt Relief: How Intermediary Liquidity Shapes Mortgage Buyouts
entry.summary: The Financing of Debt Relief: Intermediary Liquidity and the Value of Borrower Information arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper studies how intermediary liquidity affects mortgage resolution, using 1.9 million Ginnie Mae buyout options from 2019 to 2022. When funding markets froze in 2020, nonbank issuers repurchased far fewer delinquent loans than depositories servicing loans in the same pools, and shifted away from large balances. About $19 billion of repurchases were delayed, and most were completed later.

entry.title: Multi-period mean-expectile portfolio optimization under Wasserstein ambiguity, with reformulation and ground-metric effects
entry.summary: Multi-period Mean-Expectile Portfolio Optimization under Wasserstein Ambiguity: Reformulation, Degeneracy and the Role of the Ground Metric arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper studies multi-period portfolio optimization using expectiles as the risk measure under Wasserstein ambiguity sets. The authors derive an envelope theorem that characterizes the worst-case expectile as the unique root of a worst-case expectation, enabling standard Wasserstein duality and a reformulation into four parametric linear programs. Experiments on 90 FTSE constituents over 3,341 out-of-sample trading days show the expectile model outperforms a matched CVaR model in all nine parameter cells.

entry.title: Weighted selection from elliptical distributions: a stochastic representation for portfolio separation
entry.summary: Weighted selection from elliptical distributions: a stochastic representation and an application to portfolio separation arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper represents weighted-selection elliptical distributions as an affine combination of q selection variables plus an elliptical term whose direction alone is independent. This representation suffices for q+2 fund separation via first-order stochastic dominance. It relaxes the three-fund assumptions of Simaan (1993).

entry.title: A Hawkes-based microfoundation for a multitype inverse-Gaussian random clock
entry.summary: A Hawkes Microfoundation for Multitype Inverse Gaussian Subordinators arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper derives a multitype inverse-Gaussian subordinator as the limit of event counts and integrated intensities of nearly critical multivariate linear Hawkes processes. The limit is a multivariate pure-jump subordinator whose dependence comes from microscopic cross-excitation. In the diagonal case it reduces to independent classical inverse-Gaussian subordinators. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an event-level Hawkes microfoundation showing joint convergence of counts and integrated intensities to a multitype inverse-Gaussian subordinator, explain the mechanism via clusters b

entry.title: Linking Stochastic Differential Equations to a Hierarchy of Generalized Beta Distributions
entry.summary: From a Hierarchy of Stochastic Differential Equations to a Hierarchy of Generalized Beta Distributions arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper introduces a mean-reverting stochastic differential equation with a three-component noise term that generates a hierarchy of stationary distributions. The top level is a modified-Beta distribution, and its one- and two-parameter reductions yield compact-support, power-law, and exponential-type families. The authors build two generalizations, applying a power transformation either before or after obtaining the stationary hierarchy, and show these routes agree on some lower branches but generally differ at the top level. They derive density and distribution functions for both routes and compare them with the traditional Generalized Beta framework.

entry.title: A study revisiting Bonart's explanation of the square-root impact law
entry.summary: On Bonart's interpretation of the Square-Root Impact Law arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 This paper examines theoretical explanations of the square-root impact law, which links price impact to the square root of traded volume. The authors reformulate Bonart's argument based on diffusive prices and white increments, emphasizing that the market must whiten each participant's stationary stream of metaorders rather than isolated ones. They build a multi-agent propagator model and note that its falsifiable prediction, that isolated metaorders should not follow the law, seems at odds with known empirical data.

entry.title: Robust portfolio risk management using CVaR with a reward-penalty mechanism
entry.summary: Conditional value-at-risk under reward-penalty mechanism with applications to robust portfolio management arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 This paper proposes robust portfolio selection models that add a reward-penalty mechanism to portfolio management, assuming the joint loss distribution of risky assets is uncertain but lies within a multivariate distribution set. It derives an explicit closed-form expression for the worst-case conditional value-at-risk and uses it to find allocations that minimize this worst-case CVaR. Experiments with real market data suggest the models can outperform several existing related models, and that combining downside risk with portfolio loss can improve risk management and returns. The results also show a trade-off between raising expected return and controlling worst-case CVaR.

entry.title: Exponential investors facing weakly mean-reverting prices
entry.summary: Exponential investors with weakly mean-reverting prices arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 This paper studies a continuous-time market where asset prices show weak (sublinear) mean reversion and a nonzero drift. For an investor maximizing expected exponential utility, the authors show the certainty equivalent grows as O(T^{2β+1}), where 0<β<1 is the mean-reversion strength. An explicit asymptotically optimal strategy is also provided.

entry.title: Convex Order in Higher Dimensions: Projection Tests, Counterexamples, and Gaussian Mixtures
entry.summary: Convex Order Beyond Dimension One: Projection Tests, Counterexamples and Gaussian Mixtures arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper studies convex order, a way to compare random vectors with the same mean, in dimensions greater than one. It shows that checking all one-dimensional projections is not sufficient in general and builds radial counterexamples in every dimension at least two. The authors prove that projection tests do suffice for linear transformations of a common radially distributed vector, including centred Gaussian distributions. They also settle when a centred Gaussian is dominated by a mixture of two centred Gaussians, showing this holds exactly when all one-dimensional projections are ordered. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that projection tests are necessary and sufficient for multivariate convex order between a centred Gaussian and a two-component centred Gaussian mixture, and construct radial countere

entry.title: Continuous Latent Stress Spectrum in Limit Order Book Dynamics
entry.summary: Latent Continuum of Regimes in Limit Order Book Dynamics arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 The paper analyses high-frequency limit order book data for EURO STOXX 50 index futures over 987 trading days from 2022 to 2025, testing whether market states form distinct regimes or a continuum discretised into apparent regimes. It finds an effective state dimension of about 1.4, with one dominant latent coordinate explaining 83.66% to 85.27% of covariance-state variation and tracking VSTOXX without regime labels. Fine-scale continuous information remains predictive, with forecasting peaking near ten minutes and a maximum pooled out-of-sample R2 of 0.7483. ★★★★ Notable: Using Riemannian geometry, the authors argue limit-order-book states form a continuum rather than discrete regimes; across 987 trading days and 17 methods, the dominant coordinate explains 83.66%–85.2

entry.title: Error bounds for option pricing under volatility uncertainty
entry.summary: A posteriori error bounds for the Uncertain Volatility Model arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 The paper develops a posteriori primal-dual bounds for numerical approximations of European option prices in the Uncertain Volatility Model. A lower bound comes from a feedback control induced by the Hessian of a smooth candidate value function, while an upper bound comes from a dual representation based on a matrix-valued Gamma field. The authors also quantify discretization errors and test candidates from policy-gradient and physics-informed neural networks. The experiments indicate that second-order derivative accuracy is important for tight bounds.

entry.title: Measuring Trade Direction on a Prediction Market: Settlement-Based Validation and Trading-Cost Measurement on Polymarket
entry.summary: Measuring Trade Direction in a Prediction Market: Settlement Ground Truth and Trading-Cost Measurement on Polymarket arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper validates the trade-direction labels of Polymarket's public trade prints against the taker leg of on-chain settlement records. It compares Lee-Ready, tick-test and retrospective bulk volume classification, and shows how sign errors shift measured effective spread, realised spread and midpoint impact. The authors caution that these delivered-quote accounting measures do not identify causal impact or private information.

entry.title: Comparing run-off triangles and regression for estimating credit card loss given default
entry.summary: Comparing two approaches for modelling the loss given default of credit cards: Run-off triangles vs regression arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 The paper benchmarks run-off triangles, a common banking method, against a two-stage regression model for estimating credit card loss given default (LGD). The regression approach can reproduce the typical U-shaped LGD distribution, which run-off triangles cannot. Aggregated regression estimates also track empirical loss rates over time much more closely. The authors suggest the regression approach is likely better under IFRS 9, which prioritises accuracy.

entry.title: A Dirichlet mixed-membership model for exact multivariate credibility in insurance pricing
entry.summary: A Dirichlet Mixed-Membership Model for Exact Multivariate Distributional Credibility arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper proposes a Dirichlet mixed-membership model (DMMM) that represents policyholder risk as a stable composition over latent risk classes. Baseline characteristics set the a priori assessment, and repeated multivariate experience updates the a posteriori assessment. The posterior predictive distribution is written exactly as a convex combination of portfolio and experience components, extending classical credibility beyond the conditional mean. The framework is studied through a simulation and a vehicle telematics application.

entry.title: Speculative Imbalance Positions by Non-Physical Traders and Their Effect on Great Britain's Electricity Balancing
entry.summary: Speculative Imbalance Positions by Non-Physical Traders: Impacts on Electricity System Balancing in Great Britain arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper provides the first empirical analysis of speculative imbalance positions taken by non-physical traders in Great Britain's electricity system from 2021 to 2024. Using counterfactual simulations that remove the aggregate non-physical trader imbalance, the authors measure effects on balancing volumes, balancing costs and supplier imbalance costs. They find these positions reduced balancing costs by 5.9 to 6.7 percent and supplier imbalance costs by 65 to 75 percent, suggesting consumer bills would have been higher without them.

entry.title: AlphaRLM: Training Language Models to Build Market Factors from Finance Literature
entry.summary: AlphaRLM: Aligning Language Models for Literature-Grounded Symbolic Factor Discovery arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper introduces AlphaRLM, a reinforcement-learning framework that trains LLMs to construct executable symbolic trading factors directly from financial literature, without requiring input factor expressions. It combines Literature-Guided Operator Assembly (LEGO) with rewards for executable validity and grouped-return separation. Experiments on CSI 300, CSI 1000, and S&P 500 report that AlphaRLM outperforms several factor-mining and LLM-based baselines in annualized excess return.

entry.title: Too Late to Prune: How Timing of Generative AI Access Affects Team Creative Choices
entry.summary: Too Late to Prune: Generative AI, the Screen, and Team Creative Decisions arXiv · Oct 11, 2026 This paper examines when generative AI's options are most valuable to creative teams. In a randomized experiment, 148 three-person teams used the same language model at different stages of a timed product-design task. Moving the same 15 minutes of access from the search stage to the selection stage lowered expert-rated creativity by 0.62 standard deviations, with the difference located at the screening step.

entry.title: Exact phase-type point processes for measuring and predicting event streams
entry.summary: Exact Phase-Type Point Processes for Certified Measurement and Prediction of Event Streams arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 The paper proposes a point-process framework built on a phase-type (Erlang-chain) state space, giving exact likelihoods for both measuring market reactions and predicting the next event. Applied to six markets around 670 scheduled macroeconomic releases from 2022 to 2026, the measurement model finds that the direct reaction to CPI, payrolls, PPI and the FOMC statement is absorbed in about a second, while the market's own echoes stretch half the response to 16-137 seconds. The prediction model, EPT-X, is reported to achieve the best test likelihood on several event-stream datasets and to match the best published model on StackOverflow. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a multiscale phase-type Hawkes process with a concave likelihood, a duality-gap certificate for the global optimum, and closed-form shock responses with a stability criterion, appl

entry.title: Early warning of pension sponsor distress using public filings and dynamic investment limits
entry.summary: Early Detection of Pension-Sponsor Distress from Public Filings: A Sponsor Vulnerability Index, Stress-Augmented VaR, and Dynamic Self-Investment Caps arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper presents a transparent early-warning pipeline built on public data, centred on a Sponsor Vulnerability Index (SVI) that uses SEC EDGAR balance-sheet fundamentals and two macro series. On 36 U.S. sponsors (1,418 firm-quarters), it reaches an out-of-fold AUC-ROC of 0.887 under leave-one-firm-out validation. It also adds a stress-augmented Monte Carlo VaR and a self-investment cap that falls as the SVI signals distress, and reports the method's failure modes.

entry.title: CorrFlow: Exact, permutation-equivariant generation of valid correlation matrices via flow matching
entry.summary: CorrFlow: Exact and Permutation-Equivariant Flow Matching on the Correlation Elliptope arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper presents CorrFlow, a method for generating correlation matrices that separates keeping outputs valid from learning the data distribution. A generalized Fisher transform maps correlation matrices to unconstrained coordinates, where a graph flow-matching network learns the empirical distribution and is permutation equivariant. On 80×80 Taiwan equity matrices, CorrFlow produced 100% valid draws without repair and a lower feature sliced-Wasserstein distance than CorrGAN and image diffusion. The authors note the results do not establish superiority over fully tuned image models or isolate each component's contribution.

entry.title: Selecting Sparse Features for Financial Regression Using Monte Carlo Tree Search
entry.summary: L₀ Feature Selection via Monte Carlo Tree Search in High-Dimensional Financial Regression arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper proposes a feature selection method for high-dimensional financial regression that uses Monte Carlo Tree Search with Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation. Candidate feature subsets are scored by out-of-sample validation performance rather than training error. On a task explaining weekly NASDAQ-100 returns from 1,072 engineered features, the method reaches an out-of-sample R² of 0.6961, compared with 0.6313 for an optimized Lasso baseline.

entry.title: How AI shopping assistants affect retail revenue and product range choices
entry.summary: AI-Mediation in Retail Markets: Revenue Effects and Assortment Optimization arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper studies how a retailer should choose its product range when AI shopping assistants shape which items customers consider. Ignoring AI mediation is shown to cause average revenue losses of 2.52% to 11.37% relative to the Plackett-Luce optimum, while a simple deterministic approximation based on fitted AI utility orderings loses at most 0.53% on average. The authors also prove that, for a fixed number of customer segments, the optimization problem admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

entry.title: A distributional framework for characterizing and managing risk in large language models by measuring how their repeated responses vary.
entry.summary: A Distributional Framework for Behavioral Characterization and Risk Management of Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper notes that large language models are inherently stochastic, so repeated runs under identical conditions can yield different responses. It proposes a framework applicable across the model lifecycle, estimating empirical response distributions via Monte Carlo simulation and studying how they shift under semantic interventions. The authors illustrate it with borrower classification and music album recommendation tasks, linking it to model risk management by measuring robustness and control effectiveness. Because it relies only on observed responses, it can also be applied to black-box models accessed through commercial APIs.

entry.title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models: A causal simulator trained on synthetic markets estimates how large trades causally move prices.
entry.summary: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper presents a proof-of-concept Causal Market Simulator, a continuous-time causal PFN trained on a synthetic market where hidden informational flow confounds flow and price. On this prior, the naive estimator's bias follows a closed form (up to 68% overestimation), and the model tracks the unbiased oracle at high confounding. The authors report zero-shot responses to metaorders in an ABIDES order book and to flow bursts in crypto perpetuals and Nasdaq equities, consistent with but not proof of causal transfer. A recurrent state-space variant better captures impact accruing over execution duration.

entry.title: Forecasting Resale Prices of Used Phones and Laptops: A Benchmark of Statistical and Deep Learning Models
entry.summary: Deep Learning vs. Statistical Models for Multi-Horizon Price Forecasting of Second-Hand Electronics: A Systematic Benchmark arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper presents the first multi-horizon benchmark for predicting resale prices of used smartphones and laptops. Using daily listing data from Polish online marketplaces (January 2022 to March 2025), it compares eleven statistical and deep learning models across horizons from 1 to 365 days. N-BEATS achieves the lowest error beyond 30 days, with a MAPE of 8.51% at 365 days versus 14.94% for the best statistical baseline. At 1 to 7 days, all models perform similarly and a naive baseline remains competitive.

entry.title: SOTA: Option-Implied Return Distribution-Guided Stock Options Trading Agents
entry.summary: SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper presents SOTA (Stock Options Trading Agents), an agentic framework that selects structured option strategies by abstracting the large contract universe into strategy-level decisions, with deterministic resolvers handling implementation. It post-trains Qwen3.8-27B using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.
