Evaluated on options for nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY against rule-based and machine-learning selectors, SOTA reports an 18.3% six-month out-of-sample return, a Sharpe ratio of 1.60, and an 8.96% maximum drawdown. The authors also find news plays an asymmetric role: it improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning lowers out-of-sample return to -2.7%.

entry.title: OOM-RL II: Reality as Oracle, Not Debugger — Provenance-Constrained Diagnosis in Evolving Agent-Engineered Systems
entry.summary: OOM-RL II: Reality Is an Oracle, Not a Debugger Provenance-Constrained Diagnosis in Continually Evolving Agent-Engineered Systems arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper examines a human-directed, agent-engineered quantitative trading system to show what external outcome feedback can and cannot establish. Over one year the account gained and beat a broad market index, yet annual alpha was not statistically distinguishable from zero under the main retrospective specification, and engineering records show changes during the period with incomplete recommendation-to-runtime binding. The authors introduce an outcome–diagnosis gap, distinguish frozen instances, pre-specified adaptive procedures, and ad-hoc development, and propose a prospective production-binding protocol that has not yet been prospectively validated.

entry.title: DSTNet: A Causal Multi-Horizon Forecasting Model for Financial Time Series
entry.summary: DSTNet: Dynamic Spectral Trajectory Network for Causal Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 DSTNet is a forecasting model that keeps the recent evolution of wavelet filter-bank magnitudes from seven technical indicators over a twenty-day lookback, using only causal information. It outputs one, three, five, and ten day forecasts in one pass. Tested on seven equity indices and gold against nine learned baselines and a random-walk benchmark, it beats persistence only at longer horizons in MAE and MAPE, while one-day results are inconclusive. A downstream allocation test does not show an equity-timing advantage.

entry.title: Residual Learning for Deeper Neural Asset Pricing Models
entry.summary: Residual Learning in Empirical Asset Pricing arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 This paper applies residual learning to neural network asset pricing models, preserving and refining shallow benchmark models so that the networks can be made deeper. Out of sample, value-weighted long-short portfolios built from deep residual models achieve a Sharpe ratio of 2.07, versus 1.92 for the corresponding shallow models and 0.89 for deep feedforward models. The authors conclude that model depth provides additional economic value in asset pricing and that the approach can scale such models.

entry.title: FinVector-Market-4B: a controlled test of LoRA tuning for structured finance tasks
entry.summary: FinVector-Market-4B: A Controlled Study of LoRA Adaptation for Structured Financial Tasks arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper fine-tunes the Qwen3.5-4B model with rank-16 LoRA on 22,000 examples for structured financial tasks, then compares it with the base model on a 600-example benchmark. Supplying a JSON schema alone raised the base model's JSON validity from 0% to 91.3%. Under matched explicit prompting, several task scores also improved. The authors note that the reported macro-F1 drop reflects a changed label set, and that filing overlap and other issues limit the generalization claims.

entry.title: Learned Monotone Recurrent Features in Regulated Credit Scoring
entry.summary: Learned Monotone Recurrent Features in Governed Credit Scoring: The Price of the Frame and the Necessity of Macro Conditioning arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper examines whether learned monotone recurrent features add value to regulated credit scoring, testing five production-scale credit datasets. The authors extend the monotonicity guarantee with proofs to vector inputs and macro-conditioned decay gates. They find that learned feature value rises with governance strictness, and that conditioning the recurrence on macroeconomic series, rather than using them as inputs, yields crisis-cohort AUC gains.

entry.title: Adversarial training for deep hedging when markets shift over time
entry.summary: Adversarial Training for Deep Hedging in Nonstationary Markets arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper proposes WRAP, a drift-aware adversarial training framework for deep hedging based on a two-budget distributionally robust optimization formulation. It lets an adversary reweight observed trading trajectories under a φ-divergence constraint and perturb their paths under an optimal-transport constraint, to handle mismatch between historical training data and future market conditions. Experiments on stationary and nonstationary Heston dynamics and a generalized affine diffusion (GAD) show that reweighting and transport each help, with joint adversarial training giving the largest gains under nonstationarity.

entry.title: Expert-verified AI study materials and who gains from them in a university course
entry.summary: Verified, not generated: expert-verified AI study materials and the distribution of learning gains in a university course arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper studies a compulsory first-year economics course in which one cohort received AI-generated podcasts, FAQs and quiz-based study guides checked by a graduate teaching assistant. A difference-in-differences analysis of 340 examination marks links access to a 2.34-mark average advantage on a 50-mark component. Most of the average effect originates in the bottom quintile, and the authors argue that evaluations reporting only mean effects cannot show whether the intended students benefit.

entry.title: Synthetic cultural agents built from group-level preference anchors
entry.summary: Synthetic Cultural Agents from Aggregate Anchors arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 The paper proposes building synthetic survey respondents by mapping the signs of six Global Preferences Survey coordinates to group-specific choice policies, each fitted as a parameter-efficient adapter with Direct Preference Optimization. On candidate World Values Survey items, the adapters recover the imposed labels and separate the two GPS-sign groups on a sixteen-country development panel. However, agreement between the adapters and human WVS responses remains unresolved.

entry.title: Who Keeps the Gains from AI Assistants? Seller Responses and Non-Users in a Simulated Rental Market
entry.summary: Who Keeps the Gains from Personal AI Assistants? Seller Adaptation and the Unassisted in a Language-Model Market Simulation arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper uses an agent-based rental market simulation with language models to study how sellers' responses shape the gains from personal AI assistants and their effects on consumers without one. With frozen sellers, executing assistants cut adopters' spending by 13.7 USD per renter-day, and adaptation recovered about a third. The predicted burden on non-users did not materialise, with a mean spending change near zero. The authors argue assistants should be evaluated at the market level. ★★★★ Notable: Agent-based language-model market simulation shows seller adaptation claws back about a third of assistant gains, and the unassisted burden forecast fails.

entry.title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets: a study of arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts
entry.summary: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper develops a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage among logically related prediction-market contracts, proving that prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage and using integer programming to find optimal arbitrage portfolios. Using venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria, the authors recover 1.9 million logical relations covering more than 255,000 contracts. Replaying full-depth Polymarket order books, they find that an ideal arbitrageur earns a risk-free return of 3.5% a week on settled portfolios after spreads and fees. Opportunities persist longer and attract less observed participation where relation discovery and execution are more costly.

entry.title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-Risk Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
entry.summary: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-Risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 This paper studies Markov decision processes whose objective is Value-at-Risk (VaR), a quantile-based risk measure. Earlier work gave dynamic programming equations for finite state and action spaces, but the general case was unresolved. The authors show these equations are valid in continuous spaces, for both finite and infinite horizons. They apply the framework to an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and characterize the optimal dynamic strategies.

entry.title: GROMM: A risk-neutral option market model that fits European option prices without arbitrage.
entry.summary: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 The paper presents a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free model of European option markets, built on the SANOS framework to smoothly interpolate option prices, and proves its dynamics have a unique strong solution. It serves as a stochastic local volatility representation of an option price surface rather than a pricing model. Tested on S&P Index option data from January 2022 to August 2025, the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for over 95% of relevant prices. The authors also propose a range of BHW tests for checking the absence of arbitrage.

entry.title: Dynamic portfolio selection using range VaR and log returns
entry.summary: Dynamic portfolio selection under range value-at-risk with logarithmic returns arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 This paper studies continuous-time portfolio selection in which risk is measured by Range Value-at-Risk (RVaR) and performance is evaluated using logarithmic returns. The dynamic problem is reduced to a static quantile problem, and the optimal terminal wealth is characterized through a convex envelope. The RVaR solutions reduce to their VaR and Expected Shortfall counterparts in limiting parameter cases.

entry.title: Optimal trading filters and how much predictive signals are worth in trading
entry.summary: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 The paper solves a quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using Wiener-Hopf factorization. The optimal policy is expressed as a conditional forecast composed with an explicit causal linear filter. Results are given for exponential resilience and power-law impact decay, and the net value under trading costs is characterized. ★★★★ Notable: Uses Wiener-Hopf factorization to derive optimal trading under transient impact, yielding fractional trading filters and characterizing value with and without trading costs, mainly for quantitative fi

entry.title: Rachev-Ratio Portfolio Allocation Using TimeGAN-Generated Scenarios: Replacement Versus Supplementation
entry.summary: Rachev-Ratio Portfolio Optimization with TimeGAN Scenarios: Replacement versus Supplementation arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 This study tests how well scenarios from a TimeGAN model work in portfolio allocation using 12 exchange-traded funds. It compares historical, replacement, and hybrid policies across five training seeds, with delayed execution and transaction costs included. The generated scenarios understate volatility and tail losses and distort dependence between assets, and longer training improves reconstruction loss without improving correlation accuracy. Some hybrid configurations earn higher average net returns, but the confidence intervals for generated-versus-historical differences include zero at the reference block length.

entry.title: Choosing Trade Duration and Execution Schedule Under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
entry.summary: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 This paper studies order execution under concave power-law market impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations. It selects the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L, then derives the execution schedule shape via convex programming. The authors report that an interior optimal horizon exists only under certain sign conditions, and the objective is nearly flat over a wide window. Under Hurst-scaled cost, the schedule is front-loaded and tapers smoothly to zero, saving 10-17% of envelope cost versus a constant-rate (TWAP) schedule.

entry.title: Modelling Cross-Product Liquidity in Intraday Electricity Markets with Hawkes Processes
entry.summary: Cross-product Modelling in Continuous Intraday Electricity Markets via Hawkes Processes arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 This paper introduces a multivariate State-Dependent Hawkes Process to model how Quarter-Hourly and Hourly intraday continuous electricity contracts influence each other's liquidity. Trading sessions are split into 'Normal' and 'Stressed' regimes using bid-ask spread, mid-price volatility and queue imbalance. The model is calibrated on level 3 limit order book data from the Dutch EPEX SPOT market for the first month of each quarter of 2024. Results show roughly 95% of orders are reactions to earlier orders, and under stress the leadership of the Quarter-Hourly contract weakens while the cross-contract lag shrinks sharply.

entry.title: Basis-Only Funding Is Not Dividend Fair: Settlement Design for Crypto Equity Perpetuals
entry.summary: Basis-Only Funding Is Not Dividend Fair: Settlement Design in Crypto Equity Perpetuals arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper examines perpetual futures on dividend-paying equities listed on crypto venues. It argues that the common premium-index funding mechanism, which sets funding from the basis, cannot replicate shareholder cash flows for traders entering and exiting at arbitrary times, because funding serves both basis control and settlement. A predictable dividend behaves as a measure-theoretic atom, so fairness requires a discrete event-based settlement. Exchange-native data are cited to show one venue posts such a discrete funding payment at ex-dividend dates while a standard venue does not.

entry.title: Collusion Without Deterrence: Auditing Punishment in Q-Learning Pricing
entry.summary: Algorithmic Collusion Without Deterrence: Auditing the Punishment Mechanism in Q-Learning Pricing Agents arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 The paper replicates a simulated Bertrand duopoly in which independent Q-learning pricing agents converge to above-competitive prices. Auditing frozen policies, the authors find the reward-punishment explanation does not hold: a single attractor covers most of the state space, and re-pairing agents collapses coordination by 80%. They also report that the one-period undercut is unprofitable in 92% of pairs, but optimal deviations earn 17.5% on average, so collusion persists largely because deviation is never attempted. ★★★★ Notable: Frozen-policy audits question the punishment-mechanism account of algorithmic collusion: one-period undercuts are unprofitable in 92% of pairs, yet dynamic-programming optimal deviations profit 17.5%

entry.title: Executed and Recoverable Credit: How Action Order Shapes LLM Borrowing in a Simulated Lending Market
entry.summary: Requested, Executed and Recoverable Credit: Shared Action Ordering among LLM Borrowers in a Simulated Lending Market arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 This paper tests whether the order in which shared actions occur changes how much credit is actually executed in a simulated collateralized lending market with three small open-weight language models. An exact randomization test rejects the claim that common-market net debt is unaffected by complete-order assignment (two-sided p = 2/8,100). All 24 markets increased debt, and no market experienced liquidation or realized bad debt. The authors also report that reference-priced collateral narrows the observed order gap under fixed requests.

entry.title: Six Gaps Between Backtests and Live Trading in an Intraday System
entry.summary: Where Backtests and Live Trading Part Ways: Six Defects from One Intraday System arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 The paper reports six defects found by comparing a US equity intraday trading system's live days with its backtest replay. Three stem from data issues, two from code, and one from configuration. For each defect, the authors describe the symptom, error size, cause, and the test or control now used to prevent it. The paper makes no claim about whether the system is profitable.

entry.title: Valuing American commodity options with a two-factor price model and an efficient numerical scheme
entry.summary: Pricing American Commodity Options Under the Schwartz Two-Factor Model Using the Alternating Direction Explicit (ADE) Method arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 This paper studies how to value American commodity options under the Schwartz two-factor model. It uses a double-sweep alternating direction explicit (ADE) finite difference method and compares it with Saul'yev's single-sweep variant. The authors derive the governing PDE, map the semi-infinite domain to a rectangle, and set boundary conditions using Fichera theory. The solver is checked against a closed-form European solution and Monte Carlo, then benchmarked against Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo for accuracy and convergence. Following feedback from a commodities trader, the framework was extended to exercise on futures prices and to use seasonal parameters.

entry.title: Loss-versus-rebalancing with external transaction costs
entry.summary: Loss-versus-rebalancing with external proportional transaction costs arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 This paper studies liquidity provision in automated market makers when trading on external markets incurs proportional transaction costs. It compares the pool with a self-financing benchmark that holds the same risky inventory and trades at external bid and ask prices. Under continuous prices and pure arbitrage, the two have identical liquidation wealth whenever the pool fee or external spread is positive. The paper also constructs pool designs that implement decreasing inventory schedules and constant no-trade boundaries.

entry.title: Neural Estimation of Irreversibility in Market Order Book Paths
entry.summary: Neural Estimation of Irreversibility in Real and Simulated Limit Order Book Paths arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 The paper defines a time irreversibility rate for coarse-grained limit order book paths as the forward-to-reverse log-density ratio per event. It estimates this rate from three weeks of Nasdaq order data using order-invariant and order-sensitive neural networks. Real paths show more irreversibility than a surrogate preserving the one-step transition table, while a calibrated queue-reactive simulator matches the overall rate but shows almost no ordering-based increment. The authors propose the ordering and scale profile of path irreversibility as a benchmark for order book simulators.

entry.title: Regime Detection in Latent Factor Models: A Bayesian Decision-Theoretic Approach
entry.summary: Regime Detection in Latent Factor Models -- A Bayesian Decision-Theoretic Approach arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 This paper studies when an agent should act on inferred regime changes in models with latent factors and hidden regimes. It frames online regime detection as a Bayesian decision problem that balances false alarms, detection delay, and misclassification, solved approximately with particle filtering and Monte Carlo dynamic programming. In numerical experiments on Heston and regime-switching Vasicek models, the latent-information procedure outperforms feasible plug-in rules.

entry.title: Data-driven dynamic portfolio selection using vine copula simulation and reinforcement learning
entry.summary: Data-Driven Dynamic Portfolio Selection with Vine Copula Simulation and Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper proposes a dynamic portfolio selection method that combines vine copula simulation with reinforcement learning, for an investor with constant relative risk aversion who penalises conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of losses. A conditional vine model is fitted to historical returns to generate scenarios and paths for training a recurrent portfolio policy, and stability bounds are derived for parameter errors. On a seven-asset panel of US and Chinese equities and gold, an ensemble of ten trained policies reports a 34.13% compound annual growth rate and a Sharpe ratio of 2.31 over 22 monthly holding periods, exceeding six benchmarks.

entry.title: The Missile and the Toll: Two-Way Flow Through the Strait of Hormuz
entry.summary: The Missile and the Toll: Two-Way Flow Through the Strait of Hormuz arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper models a Stackelberg escalation game in which an enforcer picks an attack intensity and a toll schedule for the Strait of Hormuz, while ships choose to pay, cross exposed, wait, reroute, or exit. The authors argue that attacks create willingness to pay and tolls capture it. The model predicts asymmetry across trade types. Payments would be clandestine, but its implications can be tested against freight rates, insurance premia, and incident reports.

entry.title: A GLE-LSV model with state-dependent leverage and colored noise
entry.summary: A GLE-LSV model with state-dependent leverage and colored noise arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper studies a local stochastic volatility model in which the variance factor follows a generalized Langevin equation with colored noise, and past returns affect variance through a memory kernel with state-dependent amplitudes. It proves existence, uniqueness, and non-explosion for kernels that are finite sums of exponentials. Under structural and nondegeneracy conditions, it shows that an exact reduced Markovian state has a smooth density, so the Dupire conditional expectation can be computed without a stochastic PDE. The paper also covers premiums under the minimal entropy martingale measure, the squared VIX, and a regularized calibration problem with bid-ask constraints.

entry.title: Risk Measures for the Climate Transition Age: Why Symmetric Risk Budgets Fall Short
entry.summary: Risk Measures for the Climate Transition Age: Why Symmetric Risk Budgets are unlikely to mitigate two-dimensionally asymmetric Climate Change risks arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper argues that common risk measures such as variance, standard deviation and tracking error penalise outperformance as heavily as underperformance, which conflicts with climate transition investing. The authors propose downside-only alternatives, including semi-variance, standard risk and trailing error. They also suggest specific mandate design changes that would let institutional investors pursue transition opportunities within risk-aware frameworks.

entry.title: Portfolio decarbonization when carbon and transition information is incomplete
entry.summary: Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper studies how an investor can dynamically decarbonize a portfolio when firms' carbon intensities and the transition state are only partly observable. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth minus a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. In a numerical example, incomplete information has limited effects when prior beliefs are well specified, but biased beliefs cause welfare losses and opposite portfolio tilts that affect the chance of exceeding the emissions target differently.

entry.title: On integrability of local utility maximizing strategies
entry.summary: On integrability of local utility maximizing strategies arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper studies local utility maximizing strategies in stochastic control, where a local optimizer is derived from a global criterion such as expected utility. The existence of such a local optimizer can be established under very mild conditions, so the key question is when it has good integrability properties. The authors show that the reasonable asymptotic elasticity condition of Kramkov and Schachermayer (1999), applied to the local utility function, plays a central role.

entry.title: Structured SDEs for Realized GARCH: A Continuous-Time Volatility Model
entry.summary: Structured SDEs for Realized GARCH: Continuous-Time Volatility Modelling and Component-Level Analysis arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper proposes a continuous-time stochastic volatility model for forecasting next-day integrated variance. It feeds a jointly evolving realized-measure state into latent variance dynamics and adds correlated Brownian innovations linked to returns. Parameters are estimated via simulation-based predictive learning, with Monte Carlo simulation used for forecasts. Across 17 equity indices, the model shows strong out-of-sample performance against several benchmarks, with realized-measure feedback contributing most of the gain and return-linked Brownian dependence adding smaller complementary improvements.

entry.title: Backtesting Expected Shortfall without VaR forecasts in time-series models
entry.summary: E-Backtesting Expected Shortfall without Value-at-Risk Forecasts under Time-series Models arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper proposes two e-backtesting methods for Expected Shortfall that use only observed losses and ES forecasts, with no Value-at-Risk forecast required. One targets iid losses, and the other targets time series with an AR-GARCH conditional VaR structure. Under the stated assumptions, both methods control false rejections at any stopping time. Simulations and an application to daily NASDAQ losses compare the methods with VaR-ES e-processes and fixed-sample ES backtests. ★★★★ Notable: The paper proposes sequential e-backtests for Expected Shortfall that use only observed losses and ES forecasts, with no VaR forecast needed, extending the approach to AR-GARCH conditional VaR time se

entry.title: Designing Independent Variation: Guided Iteration for Price Experiments in Correlated Panels
entry.summary: Designing Independent Variation: A Guided Iteration Methodology for Price Experiments in Short, Correlated Panels arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper argues that estimation error in short, correlated pricing panels is driven mainly by trajectory dispersion rather than sampling noise, so only independently assigned price variation can resolve the identification shortfall. It proposes a guided iteration method that uses a cyclic price-perturbation scheme under a revenue-at-risk budget to decide how much variation to generate, where, and for how long. The method is applied to Dominick's retail data, with theoretical results and empirical comparisons reported.

entry.title: Dirichlet sub-mixtures: a new view of multiplicative risk models with Pareto margins
entry.summary: Dirichlet sub-mixtures: A new reading of multiplicative background risk models with Pareto margins arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 The paper builds a class of multiplicative background risk models with Pareto margins by combining Marshall-Olkin exponential and additive gamma risk factor structures, each including idiosyncratic and systemic background factors. Under an admissibility condition, the joint survival function is shown to be a finite sub-mixture of Pareto survival functions, with Dirichlet-probability weights over orderings that sum to at most one. The authors also study tail behavior, stating that asymptotic tail dependence and exceedance decay rates are governed by the gamma risk factors alone.

entry.title: The Buffett Effect: How Famous Investors' Stock Disclosures Move Markets
entry.summary: The Buffett Effect arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 This paper examines whether disclosed new stock positions by recognizable investors trigger larger abnormal returns than similar disclosures from non-recognizable managers. The authors build a recognition index from Wikipedia pageviews and news mentions and compare 24 well-known funds with 24 matched control funds from 2000 to 2025. They find a positive disclosure premium that grows with recognition, and portfolios copying the most recognized investors earn significant alpha lasting months.

entry.title: 4Cast Lab: An Open-Source App for Machine Learning and Statistical Analysis
entry.summary: 4Cast Lab: Open-Source App for Machine Learning & Statistical Analysis arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 4Cast Lab is a free, open-source application for machine learning, econometrics and statistical analysis that runs on the user's own computer without installation or programming. Its Forecasting mode trains eight learning algorithms under leakage-safe validation for time-ordered data and compares selected models with alternatives and naive benchmarks via formal tests. Its Estimation mode covers applied econometrics from robust OLS to ARIMA, VAR/VECM and GARCH. The paper describes version 4.6.2 and reports validation of 1,234 numerical results against reference libraries and NIST certified values.

entry.title: A theory model of household spending that compares with neighbors and resists cutting back, showing how group consumption shapes saving and investment decisions
entry.summary: A Mean Field Model of Consumption Inertia and Keeping Up with the Joneses arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 This paper studies how households choose consumption and investment when their well-being depends on spending relative to the population's geometric average, with spending cuts hurting more than increases help. The authors show that a mean field equilibrium exists under a weak interaction condition, and in a complete market with common risk it is an exact Nash equilibrium of the finite game. In a baseline example, ignoring inherited spending standards costs up to 17% of wealth, while small errors about the reference group cost less than 0.5%.

entry.title: From Economic Explanation to Better Machine-Learning Portfolio Performance
entry.summary: From Economic Explanation to Performance Improvement in Machine-Learning Portfolios arXiv · Oct 11, 2026 This paper proposes a local first-order attribution-propagation framework that links feature exposures in an allocation function to local sensitivities of portfolio performance metrics. The authors relate these attributions to Shapley values defined for portfolio objectives and derive statistical inference for Sharpe-ratio attributions. An attribution-guided exposure intervention can be applied after training without retraining the model. Empirically, the interventions yield statistically significant improvements in net Sharpe ratios across different model classes.

entry.title: Strategic Origins of Network Structure: Game-Graph Equilibria and Mechanistic Inference
entry.summary: Strategic Origins of Network Structure arXiv · Oct 18, 2026 The paper introduces the game-graph equilibrium, a stable rest point of a payoff-driven partner-choice dynamic analogous to Nash equilibrium, presenting network structure as the record of strategic interaction. The authors prove that two-type games have exactly four network topologies and generalize this to K^K classes for K-type interactions. They also develop a mechanistic inference method that constrains a block model to a game-theoretic manifold to recover generating dynamics from observed networks, applying it to real networks such as international trade.

entry.title: Conditional evidence weights for gradient-boosted credit models: estimation, additivity, and adverse action reasons
entry.summary: Conditional Weight of Evidence for Gradient-Boosted Credit Models: Estimation, Additivity and Its Relation to Adverse Action Reasons arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 The paper defines conditional weight of evidence, which measures how observing a credit characteristic changes default log odds once the rest of an applicant's credit record is known. Its sign shows whether the information is adverse or favorable for that applicant, and its size shows its strength. The authors estimate it with gradient-boosted trees and test accuracy in a bureau-style simulation. The measure is not an adverse action reason.

entry.title: Where Data Value Comes From: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
entry.summary: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper develops a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers to study how consumer disclosure rights shape sellers' data purchases and the platform's incentive to provide data. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure with anonymous purchasing and positive privacy costs, unilateral disclosure is unattractive in the baseline. The authors also discuss welfare effects and suggest capping anonymous offers at their no-data benchmark.

entry.title: Reading News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and Stock Returns
entry.summary: Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper builds news topics with NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on 1976–1995 text and adapted by contrastive fine-tuning, and compares it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT readers. The topics are used to forecast returns for the 1,000 largest US stocks over 2022–2024, a held-out period after training on 2013–2019 and validation on 2020–2021. The best validation-selected experiment loses money at every rebalancing frequency. An equal-weight combination of all readers and models earns a monthly net Sharpe ratio of 1.12, significant against zero but not against a price-only benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build news topics with NoLBERT, pretrained only on 1976-1995 text to avoid hindsight, compare it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT on 1.26 million 2012-2024 articles, and forecast top-1,000 US

entry.title: OrderFlowDiT: A diffusion model that forecasts limit-order supply, with better price and volume accuracy
entry.summary: OrderFlowDiT: Transport-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit-Order Supply Forecasting arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper studies how much limit-order volume will be submitted at each price over the next five minutes, given the current order book and recent order flow. It introduces OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport auxiliary loss, and a full-field evaluation framework that scores price placement, total volume, and uncertainty together. On 1,950 validation conditions across 30 U.S. equities, adding the transport loss cut full-field transport cost by 45.8% and the transport energy score by 26.1% versus mean squared error alone, with both improving for every stock.

entry.title: How language model agents change price competition
entry.summary: How language model agents reshape price competition arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 This paper studies LLM pricing agents in repeated Bertrand competition, a standard benchmark for algorithmic pricing. LLMs adapt faster than standard online learners, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. Depending on deployment choices, some agents can sustain supracompetitive prices while others move toward the competitive region, producing dynamic pricing regimes. ★★★★ Notable: The paper reports that LLM pricing agents can escape the Bertrand Nash outcome, with results depending on deployment: agents using raw market histories sustain supracompetitive prices, while those usi

entry.title: How momentum, commentary tone, and earnings surprise shape LLM financial forecasts
entry.summary: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts arXiv · Oct 16, 2026 The paper builds synthetic earnings announcements that independently vary 20-day momentum, uninformative commentary tone, and whether actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. It tests six instruction-tuned language model checkpoints from four families on 2,016 prompts each. The authors measure matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores rather than calibrated market probabilities. Tone and momentum often exceed the EPS contrast, though answer-encoding and other controls qualify these results. The study measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition, not internal reasoning or real return predictability.

entry.title: When Does “Post-Call” Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
entry.summary: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 The paper argues that financial NLP benchmarks can suffer a timing mismatch within events, where the prediction target starts before the text or audio input is complete. It proposes an Availability Contract requiring benchmarks to state the input boundary, availability evidence, outcome start, and supported claims. Applied to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms, the authors show that changing the timing proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls and changes quintiles for 28.3%.

entry.title: Auction-based allocation of routes in capacity-constrained networks
entry.summary: Auction-based allocation of routes in capacity-constrained networks arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper studies how to allocate sets of routes between end nodes in capacity-constrained flow networks with transfer costs. The authors introduce an origin-destination bidding language, where participants bid on bounded conic combinations of inlet, outlet and quantity licences, and routing is determined by a network-flow winner-determination problem. Under a restricted model, the VCG payment rule is shown to be core-stable. For the general model, where source access may depend on the individual consumer, they propose a nodal pricing rule based on shadow prices of flow-conservation constraints, which is always core-stable but not dominant-strategy incentive compatible.

entry.title: Structured neural solver for option pricing under stochastic volatility
entry.summary: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper introduces BeTINN, a structured conditional neural architecture that extends time-induced modulation with multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. It is evaluated on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, improving joint accuracy for normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics over the authors' baselines. The authors also find that validation physics loss does not fully determine derivative fidelity, so derivative-aware evaluation is recommended when sensitivities matter.

entry.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
entry.summary: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting arXiv · Oct 13, 2026 The paper has GPT-4o referee papers from the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings and compares its verdicts with publication in top finance journals over the next two years. Papers scored one standard deviation higher were about 44% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The predictive information came from judgements of correctness and exposition, not originality or significance. The authors conclude LLMs can check whether research is right but not whether it matters.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning with Hawkes-structured networks for market-making strategies
entry.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Hawkes-Structured Networks for Market Making arXiv · Oct 12, 2026 This paper studies market making when order arrivals are clustered and self-exciting, modeled with non-Markovian Hawkes processes. The authors propose a model-free reinforcement learning framework and a Hawkes-Structured Network that encodes order flow history with a learnable mixture-of-exponentials filter. Experiments with several kernel types show the network earns higher trading rewards than general-purpose neural architectures and implicitly recovers order-flow intensities.

entry.title: Dynamic industry-network survival model for mortgage default risk
entry.summary: Discrete-Time Survival Modelling with Dynamic Industrial Graphs for Mortgage Credit Risk arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 This paper proposes a discrete-time survival model that measures economic proximity by industrial composition similarity and rebuilds dynamic industrial graphs annually to capture changing cross-area dependence in mortgage default risk. It combines a conditional autoregressive process with a first-order autoregressive process and estimates the model using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation. Tested on U.S. mortgage loan-level data, the dynamic model outperforms static industrial graph specifications in in-sample fit and out-of-sample discrimination.

entry.title: StochLOB: Robust limit order book trend prediction using heavy-tailed noise in training
entry.summary: StochLOB: Heavy-Tailed Score Matching for Robust Limit Order Book Trend Prediction arXiv · Oct 15, 2026 This paper proposes StochLOB, a training-only score-matching framework that replaces the usual Gaussian noise in diffusion models with jump-Lévy and clipped α-stable noise to better reflect heavy-tailed, bursty limit order book order flow. The deployed predictor remains deterministic and needs no reverse-time diffusion sampling at inference. On chronologically held-out Coinbase LOB data, the variants stay competitive on uncorrupted BTC and altcoin horizons and improve several tail-window stress diagnostics. An exploratory A-share transfer study on Feishu data is also included.

entry.title: Scenario matching for credit dependence stress tests with correlation constraints and empirical risk bounds
entry.summary: Scenario Matching for Credit Dependence Stress Tests: Temporal correlation constraints and empirical risk bounds arXiv · Oct 26, 2026 The paper pairs two sets of simulated market and credit paths by minimizing the absolute error in temporal correlation relative to a target, with each market path matched to exactly one credit path so both full-scenario distributions are preserved. A perfect-matching test checks whether a uniform correlation-error tolerance is feasible and finds its smallest value, and further assignments yield exact empirical bounds on mean loss and exceedance probability. A synthetic bond-forward credit stress test illustrates matching precision and tail results. The method does not depend on the scenario generator and can be used to examine dependence assumptions in existing risk engines.

entry.title: Checking Whether Portfolio RL Agents Follow Their Intended Financial Goal
entry.summary: Certifying Reward Alignment in Portfolio Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 25, 2026 This paper proposes a decision audit for portfolio reinforcement learning that separates reward misspecification from learning error, checking whether a learned policy implements its stated mean-variance objective. The method is tested in controlled markets and on historical US industry portfolios. The authors report that it quantifies whether a learned decision implements its financial objective, separately from backtest performance.

entry.title: Institutional Traders' Intraday Forecasting Skill and Liquidity Provision
entry.summary: Intraday Forecasting Ability and Liquidity Provision of Institutional Traders arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This study uses high-frequency exchange data to examine how institutional traders' forecasting ability and liquidity provision relate to their proprietary intraday profits. It finds persistent forecasting skill, with flow-following strategies based on these traders' executions yielding annualized Sharpe ratios of 16 to 63 across trading frequencies. Higher forecasting ability and more passive executions within a position are both associated with higher profit and loss per matched position.

entry.title: Directionally Correct Expert Views in Portfolio Optimization
entry.summary: Directionally Correct Views in Portfolio Optimization arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper, inspired by the Black-Litterman framework, asks whether incorporating expert views improves portfolio allocation. In a simple Markowitz setting, the authors show that even a small amount of directionally correct information can materially improve investment decisions. They also discuss using entropy-based ideas to add expert views to end-to-end portfolio models. Empirically, simpler Markowitz-type models perform as well as an end-to-end model once directionally correct experts are included.

entry.title: Modeling how liquidity is distributed in concentrated-liquidity trading pools over time
entry.summary: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 The paper models how liquidity is spread across price ranges in Uniswap V3 and similar pools, using a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The equation combines an operator that keeps liquidity concentrated near the market price with an integral operator capturing redistribution from providers repositioning. The authors prove a mild solution exists and is unique, and reduce the model to linear stochastic equations for level, slope, and curvature. Calibration on three Uniswap pools shows lower active-band forecast error than a martingale benchmark on two pools consistent with the stationary specification, while the third pool's out-of-sample results suggest nonstationarity.

entry.title: Arithmetic Models for Pricing Commodity Futures, Vanilla, and Calendar Spread Options
entry.summary: Arithmetic Models for Commodity Futures, Vanilla, and Calendar Spread Options arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper proposes an arithmetic multi-factor stochastic volatility model for commodity futures and options, giving a low-dimensional Markovian representation of the futures curve and semi-closed-form prices for vanilla, basket, and calendar spread options. It is estimated with an unscented Kalman filter on WTI crude oil futures, vanilla options, and calendar spread options from 2013 to 2024. The authors find three volatility factors are needed, and that including calendar spread options improves the model's treatment of dependence between adjacent futures contracts. The arithmetic model is also reported to fit better than its geometric counterpart.

entry.title: Amortized neural filtering for calibrated posteriors in statistical arbitrage
entry.summary: Amortized Neural Filtering for Calibrated Posteriors in Statistical Arbitrage arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper addresses how statistical arbitrage trading ignores the uncertainty in estimating residual spread states. It introduces a Neural Filter Estimator trained on simulated mean-reverting paths that returns posterior distributions over each spread's latent state in one forward pass. On Korean equities, the conventional point estimate overforecasts returns by about a thousand basis points per holding period, and the amortized methods reduce that gap by roughly two to eight times.

entry.title: Probability-weighting functions from return distribution changes: three orthogonal channels and information-theoretic indices
entry.summary: Probability-Weighting Functions for Normal Tempered-Stable Laws: Orthogonal Channels and Information-Theoretic Indices arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper builds probability-weighting functions from changes between prior and posterior normal tempered-stable return distributions rather than a parametric family. Scale, skewness and tail thickness are isolated one at a time with variance held fixed, each producing a distinct sign pattern in the deviation from identity. Three information-theoretic indices summarize the distortions, and the framework is applied to S&P 500 ETF daily returns from 2015 to 2025.

entry.title: Conflicting History Hurts Foundation Model Return Forecasts
entry.summary: Conflicting History in Foundation Model Return Forecasts arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper examines how older return data can mislead foundation-model forecasters when the relationship between past and next returns changes. Across five forecasting procedures and three simulated processes, each run 1,024 times, conflicting history lowered the chance of beating a zero forecast in every higher-signal comparison. An exploratory study on 56 assets found that shortening inputs from 256 to 64 returns increased mean absolute error for every model.

entry.title: Compressing prediction market belief states with topology to forecast events
entry.summary: Topological Compression of Prediction Market Belief States for Event Forecasting arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper applies Topological Data Analysis and Persistent Homology to forecasting models built on prediction market data, testing whether market belief states form a structure whose shape offers predictive insight. The authors conclude that single-parameter persistent homology improves the predictive ability and calibrated accuracy of linear models. They also report that two-parameter multipersistence yields similar benefits for nonlinear models.

entry.title: More Mentions, Less Information? Checking Where Reddit Text Signals Come From in Volatility Forecasting
entry.summary: More Mentions, Less Information? Diagnosing Identity and Alignment in Reddit Embeddings for Volatility Forecasting arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 The paper forecasts log realized variance for stocks using frozen LLM embeddings of r/WallStreetBets posts, reaching an out-of-sample R² of 0.13. The authors test this against a HAR benchmark, text-free firm-identity controls, and shuffled day-text alignment to isolate the sources of the signal. They find most standalone fit comes from firm or firm-year information, with embeddings adding a small 1.22% MSE reduction over HAR that is largely eliminated by alignment shuffling and disappears in 2020–2022.

entry.title: Equilibria and Learning in Competitive Market Making: A game-theoretic study of market makers and a non-strategic trader, proving pure-strategy Nash equilibria exist and examining learning under discrete prices.
entry.summary: Equilibria and Learning in Competitive Market Making arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 The paper proposes a market-making game among N ≥ 2 strategic market makers and one non-strategic representative trader. Because quotes are continuous and payoffs are non-convex and discontinuous, standard finite-game and classical continuous existence results do not apply. Under minimal assumptions on the asset value distribution, the authors show at least one pure-strategy Nash equilibrium always exists, and that the equilibrium bid-ask spread widens strictly with asset value volatility. With discretized prices and an added regularity condition, they show time-averaged play of no-internal-regret learners approaches the continuous Nash price envelope as tick size vanishes.

entry.title: Joules-to-GDP: AI Economic Value per Unit of Energy
entry.summary: Joules-to-GDP: How Much Economic Value Do AI Systems Produce per Unit of Energy? arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper measures how much economic value an AI system creates per joule of energy consumed, using two metrics: net dollar value and time saving. The authors study 220 public GDPval tasks across 44 occupations, running five open-weight models locally and evaluating four accelerator types. They find that occupations and models that rank highest on success, dollar value, or time saving do not necessarily deliver the greatest economic return per joule.

entry.title: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability by Occupation and Country
entry.summary: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability across Occupations and Countries arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 The paper introduces the Agent Delegability Index (ADI), in which two language models rate all 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements against a frozen, preregistered rubric of delegation levels and barriers. Tasks are mapped to ISCO-08 occupation groups and weighted by ILOSTAT employment across 146 countries. The authors find that delegable employment rises with income, from 22.5% in low-income to 48.7% in high-income countries, and that ADI correlates strongly with existing generative AI exposure measures at the occupation level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build an AI-agent delegability index covering 146 countries, reporting delegable employment rising from 22.5% in low-income to 48.7% in high-income countries, and high correlation with pri

entry.title: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and LLMs
entry.summary: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper studies how aging financial news affects portfolio decisions, comparing keeping old news with timing information against filtering it out before selection. A fixed large language model extracts signals from public SEC disclosures, and these treatments are tested in reinforcement learning policies and LLMs that select portfolios directly. Over historical tests from 2023 to 2025, measured after trading costs, filtering old news gave the LLM the highest average net return of 18.43% per year when news delivery was delayed by four weeks, exceeding all RL strategies that used news. RL choices responded to timing information in a controlled test, but adding it showed no consistent benefit in historical returns.

entry.title: Governed self-evolution for autonomous investing: a multi-agent AI system with a protected core
entry.summary: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 The paper presents Steward, a multi-agent LLM system for autonomous investing with nine specialised agents, a seven-layer shared memory built by code, and nightly and quarterly self-review. Self-edits are blocked from an invariant core covering order arithmetic, risk rules and discipline-agent prompts. Reported results include a five-month live deployment over 102 trading days and a 2015–2026 backtest.

entry.title: LineageEvo: a method that uses factor evolution lineages to guide LLM-based mining of market prediction factors.
entry.summary: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 This paper addresses LLM-based evolutionary mining of formulaic alpha factors, where search tends to concentrate on a few structurally similar factors. The authors propose LineageEvo, which controls search at the lineage level by conditioning LLM variation on lineage-derived operator priors and by allocating search budget across lineages to limit concentration. Experiments on CSI 500 and S&P 500 report that LineageEvo achieves the strongest predictive performance on both markets, while LSPS yields a more balanced lineage distribution and broader factor pool.

entry.title: What launch-time contract details reveal about prediction-market trading volume and disputes
entry.summary: What Prediction-Market Contracts Reveal at Launch: Trading Volume and Dispute Risk arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 The paper analyzes 802,863 resolved Polymarket markets listed from January 2023 to May 2026, using only information available at listing, such as titles, descriptions, resolution sources, and metadata. Contract information predicts trading volume well, with market topic contributing the most. Performance drops sharply when platform changes and new listing formats appear in later periods. Dispute risk is ranked better than chance but is too imprecise for predicting individual disputes.

entry.title: JaxMARL-BC: Fast Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Models
entry.summary: JaxMARL-BC: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Modelling, in Seconds arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 This paper presents JaxMARL-BC, a JAX-accelerated simulator that trains MARL-BC economies 75 to 724 times faster than the reference implementation and scales to 200,000 independent learning households. The authors verify its correctness against known DSGE limiting cases and demonstrate it through a proof-of-concept calibration of an extended model with heterogeneous returns on capital, completed in two hours rather than over a month. The tool is released as open source.

entry.title: DSINC method extended beyond Heston to 3/2 and other non-affine stochastic-volatility models
entry.summary: DSINC beyond Heston: the 3/2 and other non-affine stochastic-volatility models arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 This paper extends the damped-sinc (DSINC) method for pricing American options from the affine Heston class to general one-factor stochastic-volatility models. It shows that the collapse identity, which reduces early-exercise integration to a single spectral integral, still holds for these models. Tests on 3/2, SABR, GARCH and lognormal-volatility models agree with fine finite-difference benchmarks to within one basis point of the strike.

entry.title: How a state-space model for limit order books internally represents market dynamics
entry.summary: Understanding the Inner Workings of a State-Space Foundation Model for Limit Order Books arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 The study examines what an 8.2M-parameter Mamba-3 state-space model learns after being trained autoregressively on tokenized limit order book message streams from eight large-cap US stocks. The authors report that order-flow imbalance is decodable from the model's internal state with R² ≈ 0.59, and that this representation extends to unseen stocks and to traded volume and volatility. They also report that steering the internal state shifts the model's next-message predictions in line with the implied feature.

entry.title: Occupational Uniqueness and Wage Growth
entry.summary: Occupational Uniqueness and Wage Growth arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper proposes a framework that separates changes in the number of tasks an occupation performs from changes in occupational uniqueness, meaning how distinct its task mix is relative to other occupations. Using 196,563 task statements from the Dictionary of Occupational Titles and O*NET covering 1977 to 2018, the authors find that occupations becoming less unique are associated with lower wage growth. The wage associations of task additions and removals depend on how widely those tasks are performed elsewhere.

entry.title: Stronger AI breakthroughs accelerate the exhaustion of their own ideas
entry.summary: Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper analyzes 36 years of computer science, including 7.2 million papers, 73,089 peer reviews and 3.7 million researchers. It finds that attention narrowed sharply after the Transformer, and that each major breakthrough was followed by steeper exhaustion of ideas. The authors call for institutions that protect diverse attention in AI. ★★★★★ Notable: Analyzing 7.2M papers, 73,089 reviews and 3.7M researchers, the authors argue breakthroughs deplete diverse attention, reporting a similar cycle in structural biology and simulations.

entry.title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Market Impact Emerging in Generative Order Book Models
entry.summary: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper introduces the LOB-Impact benchmark for testing whether generative limit order book models reproduce realistic market impact. The authors inject execution-style metaorders into order flow generated by five autoregressive models across five NASDAQ stocks and measure price responses using empirical impact estimators. Models trained only for next-token prediction show emergent impact, with exponents between 0.63 and 1.21, slightly above the square-root law's 0.5. No impact decay during relaxation was observed, which the authors tentatively attribute to short context windows; the benchmark is released as open source.

entry.title: Exact risk analysis of teacher training, fixed features, and calibration for candidate-scoring models
entry.summary: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper studies three training choices that determine what a candidate-scoring decision model's probabilities mean: soft targets from a teacher model, a frozen pretrained backbone, and temperature calibration. It analyzes these in Gaussian surrogate models where finite-sample risk can be computed exactly, and tests them on 231,521 CFPB credit card complaints about whether a complaint ends in monetary relief. The authors find that a student inherits a teacher's bias, and that calibration corrects only the probability scale, so probabilities must be checked against realized outcomes.

entry.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for market making on Polymarket order books
entry.summary: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper studies market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on Polymarket, a prediction market with thin order books. The authors reconstruct order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket and train agents on 417 real markets, splitting the maker into a quoter and a risk manager with reward shaping. Their redesigned single-agent maker quotes more often and has smaller held-out losses than the retrained baseline. However, none of the configurations achieves positive average portfolio value in periodic held-out evaluation, and each was trained with one seed.

entry.title: A Model That Ranks Market Sectors by Expected Risk-Adjusted Performance
entry.summary: Regime-Aware Interpretable Ranking for Sector Rotation arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper addresses sector rotation in benchmark-relative portfolio management by ranking sectors according to expected future risk-adjusted active performance. The authors propose RegimeRank, an interpretable model that uses expert-defined temporal signal features, conditions them on learned macro factors via cross-attention, and captures cross-sector dependencies with self-attention. On weekly S&P 500 data from 2002 to 2024, it outperforms representative ranking and machine-learning baselines across multiple ranking metrics.

entry.title: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality via Agentic Rule Discovery
entry.summary: AuDQ: Auditable Data Quality through Agentic Rule Discovery arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 The paper proposes an ontology-grounded data quality layer built into the code repository, where rules are versioned, linked to governance texts, and replayable through immutable execution traces. The authors implement the agentic rule-discovery core with Full-Agentic and Guided acquisition modes and a human-in-the-loop review interface. Preliminary experiments on finance and retail industry datasets compare whether fully autonomous divide-and-conquer rule discovery matches human expert rules in quality and diversity.

entry.title: Reconstructing Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surfaces with Additive Martingales
entry.summary: Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surface Reconstruction via Additive Martingales arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper introduces AddMart, a framework that rebuilds a continuous implied volatility surface from a few option quotes. It is designed to satisfy static no-arbitrage conditions by its architecture rather than through regularization. Tests on ten real option datasets show competitive accuracy with no material static arbitrage violations. The method also directly supports estimating VaR, CVaR, and crash probabilities.

entry.title: When Better Opportunities Backfire: How Human Workers Respond When AI Is Deployed in Parallel for Customer Acquisition
entry.summary: When Better Opportunities Backfire: Service Worker Responses to Parallel AI Deployment in Customer Acquisition arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper studies what happens when AI voice agents handle low-intent sales leads while human workers receive high-intent ones. Using over half a million outreach records from a Chinese online health-insurance brokerage and a regression-discontinuity-in-time design, the authors find that human-facing leads improve early in the workday. Yet human workers acquire fewer customers precisely where lead quality rises most, as they become less willing to persist with their current lead.

entry.title: LOBGrad: Probabilistic forecasting of limit order books using conditional diffusion models
entry.summary: Probabilistic Limit Order Book Forecasting with Conditional Diffusion Models arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 The paper introduces LOBGrad, a conditional DDPM framework that pairs an autoregressive RNN encoder with a diffusion generator to forecast limit order book dynamics probabilistically. It establishes an excess-risk oracle inequality for the one-step noise-prediction objective under exponential mixing and regularity assumptions, and shows that under contractive dynamics the dependence on conditioning-window length reduces to latent-state dimension. Experiments on BTC/USDT, GOOGL, and META show it outperforms its encoder-free diffusion ablation on all reported queue metrics and reproduces key LOB stylized facts.

entry.title: What FLARE's Published Scores Actually Measure
entry.summary: What FLARE's Published Numbers Actually Measure arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper audits the scoring pipeline of FLARE, the financial benchmark behind PIXIU and FinBen, and finds that in many cells the score depends on the answer-extraction rule rather than the model. On identical generations, two extraction rules differ in accuracy by up to 0.4216, and no leaderboard states which rule it used. The authors argue that reading a FLARE score requires ambiguity rate, coverage, and a majority-class floor, and they release floorbench to compute these from existing generations.

entry.title: Optimal investing when a green transition's timing is uncertain
entry.summary: Optimal portfolio choice under green transition timing risk arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper studies an investor's optimal portfolio choice when a possible future green transition, whose timing is uncertain, affects stock prices. The transition is modeled as a jump in which green stocks rise in value and brown stocks fall. The investor is ambiguous about timing and designs a strategy robust to this risk, with preferences that penalize ambiguity. A case study with one green and one brown stock shows that a transition-aware investor shifts holdings toward the green stock and away from the brown stock.

entry.title: Testing whether deep learning across many convertible bonds can beat simple price persistence for next-day forecasts
entry.summary: Cross-Bond Panel Learning for Next-Day Price Forecasting of Chinese Convertible Bonds: A Reality Check arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 The paper uses a daily panel of 73,806 observations from 100 Chinese A-share convertible bonds (2022–2025) to test whether cross-bond neural networks beat a random walk baseline. Under strict temporal splitting and dependence-aware inference, the price-change MLPs show slightly higher out-of-sample RMSE than the random walk, negative out-of-sample R², and non-significant test results. The authors conclude that without contemporaneous equity market information or explicit contractual event conditioning, deep panel models do not deliver next-day predictability beyond persistence.

entry.title: Building implied volatility surfaces and forecasting with survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability learning, and activity clocks
entry.summary: Compiling and forecasting implied volatility surfaces via survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper uses split-adjusted NVIDIA equity and options data from 2018 to 2025 to study how to compile implied volatility surfaces and forecast derivative risk. It combines finite-population survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks. The findings show that the sampling design should match the target measure, short-horizon prices are not forecastable beyond a random walk with drift among the tested models, and forward implied volatility shows descriptive mean-reversion that is not statistically significant under session-clustered tests.

entry.title: Measuring High-Frequency Trading in China and Its Impact on Market Quality
entry.summary: Tracking High-Frequency Trading Activity in China and Its Effects on Market Quality arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 The paper proposes an order-level proxy for high-frequency trading based on limit orders priced exactly at the best opposite-side quote. Using Shenzhen Stock Exchange data, the authors validate the proxy through its links to quote responsiveness, cancellation speed, and mid-quote returns. A difference-in-differences design using order dissemination latency differences at market open finds that lower latency raises the share of such orders, which increases short-horizon price variation, wide-spread incidence, and adverse-selection exposure. Realized spreads decline and pricing error falls modestly. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes an order-level HFT proxy based on exact-match orders and, using cross-channel latency variation at Shenzhen's open, reports that lower latency raises active exact-match shares and increases s

entry.title: Whether digital investment and energy use are reshaping the Kitchin business cycle, tested with U.S. and Irish data
entry.summary: The Digital-Energy Recomposition of the Kitchin Cycle: Exploratory Evidence from U.S. IT and Irish Data-Centre Series (1995-2025) arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 This paper uses quarterly U.S. and Irish data from 1995 to 2025 to explore whether IT investment and data-centre electricity use are reshaping the Kitchin cycle around energy and compute assets. It reports a structural break in the U.S. IT-GDP correlation in 2014Q3, and finds that the strong Irish data-centre electricity and GDP correlation largely disappears when GNP replaces GDP. The authors state that all coefficients are exploratory given small samples.

entry.title: Tokenised Sukuk: a verifiable system for asset evidence and Shariah trading rules
entry.summary: Tokenised Sukuk: A Verifiable Architecture for Asset Evidence and Programmable Shariah Compliance arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 The paper argues that security-token standards check only who holds a token, not what backs a sukuk, so an identity-only token can keep trading after non-debt assets are sold. The authors encode the 2023 Securities Commission Malaysia Shariah Advisory Council ruling on Sukuk Wakalah bi al-Istithmar as issuance and transfer policies that read signed asset evidence. In 26 scenarios on a synthetic instrument, the identity-only baseline wrongly allowed 13 operations that the full policy denies, while the full policy matched every expected outcome. ★★★★ Notable: Encodes a Malaysian Shariah ruling on sukuk tradability as on-chain policy versus identity-only baselines; across 26 synthetic scenarios the baseline wrongly allowed 13 operations at about 35,834 gas

entry.title: Deep catastrophic-risk-aware reinforcement learning: training neural policies with extreme value theory to control rare-event losses
entry.summary: Deep catastrophic-risk-aware reinforcement learning arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper extends an Extreme Value Theory approach for CVaR optimization to high-dimensional neural-network policies. It uses a peaks-over-threshold representation and method-of-moments estimation to obtain a differentiable tail-risk objective whose finite-sample gradient can be computed via automatic differentiation. In a deep-hedging study with rare extreme market moves, EVT-trained policies behaved similarly to empirical-CVaR-trained ones under normal conditions but had lower hedging losses in extreme-scenario evaluation.

entry.title: Survey on quantifying uncertainty in financial foundation models
entry.summary: Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Foundation Models: A Survey arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 This survey examines uncertainty in financial foundation models used for question answering, disclosure analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. It proposes a source-aware framework that separates six uncertainty sources across evidence and context, model and inference, and outcome and action, and a mechanism-based taxonomy for assessing methods across financial tasks. The authors map finance-specific empirical studies onto this taxonomy. They find that most studies address single parts of a workflow, with little work linking evidence and reasoning reliability to downstream prediction and constrained action.

entry.title: Prospect Theory in LLMs: Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion and Related Biases
entry.summary: Prospect Theory in Large Language Models: A Meta-Analysis of Loss Aversion, Diminishing Sensitivity, and Probability Weighting arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 This paper meta-analyzes 102 fitted estimates from 11 studies covering 32 language models to test whether LLMs show the same prospect-theory properties as people. Loss aversion is modest, with a pooled λ of 1.26, far below the strongest human estimate. Probability weighting shows a human-like inverse S shape, but diminishing sensitivity depends on the measurement method used.

entry.title: Identifying level-k reasoning in repeated games: strategies, beliefs, and cognitive ability
entry.summary: Identifying level-k reasoning in repeated games: Strategies, beliefs, and cognitive ability arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper identifies level-k reasoning operating at the level of supergame strategies in repeated games. The authors build a model covering both strategy choices and beliefs about others' strategies. Using elicited strategies and strategy beliefs from the indefinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma and a new balance-optimal error tolerance measure, they classify a substantial share of subjects as level-1 or level-2. They also find that cognitive ability and experience predict higher-level reasoning.

entry.title: Continuity of conditional distributions and stratified sampling for derivative pricing
entry.summary: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 Stratified sampling reduces Monte Carlo estimator variance by partitioning the sample space using a low-dimensional factor and sampling within each stratum, which suits path-dependent claims in high-dimensional models. The paper studies constructing neural-network stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. It establishes continuity results for conditional expectations and distributions, and gives counterexamples showing the limits of this theory. Combined with neural network density results, it yields a universal approximation theorem for admissible factors, and numerical experiments show the learned factors outperform all benchmarks considered.

entry.title: Optimal collective investment when future regulations are uncertain
entry.summary: Optimal collective investment under regulatory uncertainty arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper studies optimal collective investment under a Value-at-Risk-type constraint that reflects uncertainty about future regulatory requirements. The constraint includes several wealth thresholds and requires a minimum weighted average probability of meeting them. The authors characterize the optimal terminal wealth and show that welfare losses can be unevenly distributed among investors with different capital contributions.

entry.title: Balancing Risk Pricing, Coverage and Anti-Discrimination in Insurance Tariffs
entry.summary: Risk Adequacy and Anti-Discrimination in Insurance Pricing: Classification, Aggregation, and Transfers arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 The paper proposes a framework for insurance tariff design built on risk classification, aggregation of benchmark risk prices within classes, and balanced transfers. It evaluates tariffs on risk adequacy, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination, and frames the trade-offs as a multi-objective problem with a Pareto frontier. The authors prove several mathematical characterizations of these trade-offs and illustrate the results with a numerical motor-insurance study.

entry.title: Optimal order size for market makers under a state-dependent Hawkes process model
entry.summary: Optimal Size in Market Making under State-Dependent Hawkes Process arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 The paper models a market maker's executed volume as the product of average order size, an exponential demand function, and a Prony-series multiplier that depends on quote depth, with market-order counts built from a state-dependent Hawkes model. An empirical study on limit-order-book data examines calibrated models and sensitivity to inventory restrictions. In retrospective evaluations conditioned on realised order-flow paths, the selected calibration achieves higher terminal utility than a baseline while respecting the inventory bound, and the authors separate the effects of trading revenue from inventory control.

entry.title: Distributions or Quantiles? A Convex Theory of Worst-Case Risk
entry.summary: Distributions or Quantiles? A Convex Variational Theory of Worst-Case Risk arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 This paper develops a convex variational theory for worst-case risk evaluation using spectral risk measures, unifying and extending existing analyses. It uses a representation principle that picks the quantile or distribution formulation preserving convexity of the ambiguity set, and optimality conditions identify the worst-case law and its risk value. The theory yields closed-form or semi-closed-form solutions for several models, including Wasserstein and Kullback–Leibler ambiguity sets, and supplies projection-based algorithms with fixed-grid convergence. In a high-dimensional portfolio application, an exact projection identity under a Gaussian reference reduces robust portfolio selection to a second-order cone program. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a convex variational theory for worst-case spectral risk, deriving closed or semi-closed forms for Wasserstein and KL ambiguity sets and a portfolio SOCP reduction.

entry.title: Context-rich trading strategy using actor-critic deep reinforcement learning with sentiment for stock trading
entry.summary: Financial Context-Rich Strategy for Actor-Critic based Agents: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Stock Trading arXiv · Oct 23, 2026 This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning approach to stock trading that partially and deeply incorporates sentiment analysis to capture external factors such as social sentiment and political instability. It compares actor-critic agents using only policy optimization (A2C, PPO) with those combining policy optimization and Q-learning (DDPG, TD3, SAC). The authors report that agents combining both principles consistently improve in profit maximization and risk-averse trading when sentiment is deeply infused.

entry.title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space Under Uncertainty
entry.summary: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper proposes multichoice modeling, a framework that makes large spaces of interdependent decision configurations explicit and explorable under uncertainty. The authors treat such problems as contingent performance landscapes, drawing on rugged landscape logic, and combine variance-based sensitivity analysis with conditional distribution analysis in a single simulation. Three case studies (a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design) show how the approach reveals unexpected complementarities and near-best configurations with different risk profiles.
